src: The President was joined by a high-level business delegation and engaged the Qatari business community in various sectors with the aim of improving trade relations.
tgt: Puresidente a fambile na vahlawuriwa va mabindzu va ke henhla naswona va mburisanile mabindzu ya ke Qatar eka tisekitara to hambanahambana hi xikongomelo xo antswisa vuxaka byo xaviselana.

src: President Ramaphosa and the Amir agreed to set up working teams that will look into increasing Qatar’s investment into South Africa to match the depth of the diplomatic relations.
tgt: Puresident Ramaphosa na Amir va twananile ku endla ntlawa wo tirha lowu nga ta languta ku engetela vuvekisi bya Qatar eAfrika-Dzonga ku ringanisa vuenti bya vukaka bya matiko.

src: Geopolitical matters Cabinet reiterates the call made by African leaders for an end to the war in Gaza, during the African-Saudi Summit in Riyadh hosted by Crown Prince Mohammed Bin Salman.
tgt: 19 Timhaka ta Tipolotiki ta Misava Khabinete yi vurile nakambe xikombelo lexi endliweke hi varhangeri va Afrika xo herisa nyimpi eGaza, hi nkarhi wa Samiti ya African-Saudi eRiyadh leyi a yi khomiwe hi Crown Prince Mohammed Bin Salman.

src: The summit condemned the targeting of civilians and the violations of international law by the Israeli Government.
tgt: Samiti yi alana na ku hlaseriwa ka vaaki na ku tshoviwa ka milawu ya matiko hi mfumo wa Isirayele.

src: Cabinet continues to be concerned by the atrocities of the Israeli Government against the people of Palestine, including the deliberate attacks on the United Nations (UN) School in Gaza and the massacre of hundreds of children who had sought refuge at the school, in addition to the continued attacks on hospital staff, patients and hospital infrastructure.
tgt: Khabinete yi emahlweni yi vilerisiwa hi tihanyi ta Mfumo wa Isirayele eka vanhu va le Palesitina, ku katsa nhlaselo wa mavomu eka Xikolo xa United Nations (UN) eGaza no dlaya hi tihanyi madzana ya vana lava a va tumberile va vahlampfa exikolweni, hi ku engetela nhlaselo eka vatirhi va le swibendhlele, vavabyi na miako ya swibendhlele.

src: It is because of these continued atrocities that are being committed with impunity by the Israeli Government with the support and protection of powerful countries, that on 17 November 2023, South Africa – together with the Comoros, Djibouti, Bolivia and Bangladesh – jointly referred the situation in Palestine and Israel to the International Criminal Court (ICC).
tgt: Hikwalaho ka ku ya emahlweni ka tihanyi leti nga ku endliweni na ni xupulo hi Mfumo wa Isirayele hi ku seketeriwa no sirheleriwa hi matiko ya matimba, hi ti 17 Hukuri 2023, Afrika-Dzonga- xikan’we na Comoros, Djibouti, Bolivia na Bangladesh – hi ku katsana ya yisa xiyimo lexi xi nga ePalesitina na Isirayele eka Khoto ya Vugevenga bya Matiko ya Misava (ICC).

src: While the Palestinian Authority did ask the ICC to investigate crimes under the court’s jurisdiction in 2018, South Africa believes the current atrocities, particularly in Gaza, need renewed attention with the full backing of state parties.
tgt: Loko Nawu wa Mapelestina wu komberile ICC ku lavisisa nandzu ehansi ka Khoto ya Ndzilikani hi 2018, Afrika-Dzonga ri tshemba ku tihanyi ta sweswi ngopfungopfu eGaza, ti lava ku langutisiwa hi vuntshwa hi ku pfuniwa hi mavandla ya mfumo.

src: Our ambassador in the Hague delivered the referral in person, which asked the ICC to investigate the commission of war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide with a view to holding those most responsible accountable.
tgt: Murhumiwa wa hina eHague u yisile leswi nga rhumiwa hi yexe, leswi kombeleke ICC ku lavisisa khomixini ya vugevenga bya nyimpi, vugevenga evanhwini na ku dlaya vanhu va rixaka rin’wana ku ri nkarhi langutiwa ku khomiwa ka vanhu lava khumbekaka.

src: Given that much of the global community is witnessing the commission of these crimes in real time, including statements of genocidal intent by many Israeli leaders, we expect that warrants of arrests for these leaders, including Prime Minister Netanyahu, will be issued shortly.
tgt: Hi ku vona ku matiko ya misava yi langutile khomixini leyi ya vukhamba hi nkarhi wa kahle, ku katsa switatimende swo dlaya hi xikongomelo hi varhangeri va Isirayele vo tala, hi languterile leswaku ku va na pfumelelo wo khoma varhangeri lava, ku katsa Holobyenkulu, Netanyahu, xi ta humesiwa hi xihatla.

src: The ICC has been able to investigate the situation in Palestine since 2021 when the issue of territorial jurisdiction was settled.
tgt: ICC yi kotile ku lavisisa xiyimo xa le Palestina kusuka 2021 loko mhaka ya mindzilikano ya ndhawu yi tshamiseka.

src: However, we have noted that the Office of the Prosecutor has continued to drag its feet despite the gravity of the situation.
tgt: Hambiritano, hi vonile leswaku ofisi ya muchuchisi yi yile emahlweni no koka milenge hambi xiyimo xi vonaka xi tika.

src: The current atrocities may not have occurred if these investigations took place as soon as the Palestinian authorities first made its referral.
tgt: Tihanyi ta sweswi inge ti nga endlekaka loko vulavisisi lebyi a byi lo endliwa hi xihatla loko Vanawu va Palesitina va endlile xikombelo.

src: We expect now that other state parties have also added their voices for an end to the impunity by Israel, and the significant levels of evidence available, that international warrants of arrest will be issued by the time the Conference of Parties meet in mid-December in New York.
tgt: Hi languterile leswaku mavandla yan’wana ya mfumo yi engeterile marito yo herisa xupulo hi Isirayele, naswona xiyimo xa tikelo wa vumbhoni wu kona, leswaku xikombelo xa matiko xo nyika pfumelelo wo khoma xi ta humesiwa hi nkarhi wa Nhlengeletano ya Mavandla exikarhi ka N’wedzamhala eNew York.

src: Failure to do so will be indicative of a lack of will to act by the ICC and a strong signal to the total failure of the global system of good governance and the need to establish a new system.
tgt: Ku tsandzeka ku endla leswi swi ta kombisa ku ala ku teka goza hi ICC naswona ku tava xikombiso xo tsandzeka hi ku hetiseka ya sisitimi ya misava ya mafambiselo ya kahle no komba xilaveko xo tumbuluxa sisitimi yin’wana.

src: More children have been killed over the last month than those killed per annum in all conflicts combined for the last three years.
tgt: Vana vo tala va dlayiwile n’hweti leyi hundzeke ku tlula lava dlayiwaka hi lembe eka mintlhontlho hinkwayo yi hlanganile eka malembe manharhu lama hundzeke.

src: More UN staff members have been killed in Gaza since the founding of the United Nations.
tgt: Swirho wa UN swo tala swi dlayiwile eGaza kusukela loko United Nation yi tumbuluxiwile.

src: The numbers of journalists killed have been staggering.
tgt: Nomboro ya vateki va mahungu lava dlayiweke ya hlamarisa.

src: These are all people killed by the actions of the Israeli Government, not to defend itself, but, evinced by the statements of its leaders to clear most of Gaza of Palestinians and to occupy it.
tgt: Lava i vanhu lava dlayiweke hikwalaho ka migingiriko ya mfumo wa Isirayele, ku nga ri ku tisirhelela, kambe, ku ri xileriso swa switatimente swa varhangeri va vona xo basisa Gaza hinkwayo ya Mapalestina no tlhela va yi teka.

src: The world cannot simply stand by and watch, the global community need to rise to stop this genocide now.
tgt: Misava yi nge yimi no tlhela yi languta ntsena, matiko ya misava ya fanele ku tlakuka ya yimisa ku dlayiwa ka vanhu votala sweswi.

src: CABINET DECISIONS – including those of Special Cabinet, 9 November African Peer Review Mechanism (APRM) 20th Anniversary celebrations Cabinet considered and supported the request for South Africa to host the 20th Anniversary celebrations of the APRM from 23 to 30 November 2023.
tgt: Swiboho swa Khabinete– Ku katsa swa Khabinete yo Hlawuleka, 9 Hukuri 2023 Ku tlangela Siku ra Afrika na 20 wa Malembe ya Endlelo ro Kambisisa Tintangha ra Afrika (APRM) Khabinete yi tekela nhlokweni no seketela xikombelo xa Afrika-Dzonga xo khoma ku tlangela ka 20th wa Malembe ka APRM kusuka 23 ku fika 30 Hukuri 2023.

src: South Africa supports the APRM mission to promote the African Union’s (AU) shared values of democratic governance and inclusive development on the continent.
tgt: Afrika-Dzonga ri seketela xikongomelo xa APRM xo tlakusa African Union’s (AU) mikoka ya mafambiselo xa xidimokirasi na hluvukiso wo angarhela eka khothinete.

src: The 20th Anniversary celebrations will include the participation of current and former heads of state and government and the AU Commission.
tgt: Ku tlangela 20th wa Malembe swi ta katsa ku nghenelela ka tinhloko ta mimfumo ta sweswi na leti nga hundza na mfumo na Khomixini ya AKu tirhisiwa ka Mali kusuka eka Nkwama wa Nhlakarhelo wa Switirhisiwa swa Vugevenga (CARA) Khabinete yi pasisile ku tirhisiwa ka mali eka CARA ku lwisana na ku ceriwa ka migodi swi nga ri nawini na vugevenga byin’wana.

src: Utilisation of funds from the Criminal Assets Recovery Account (CARA) Cabinet approved the use of monies in the CARA to fight against illegal mining and other crimes.
tgt: R2 172 359 yi humesiwile ku lwisa ku ceriwa ka migodi swi nga ri nawini, leswi ya ka emahlweni swi xungeta ikhonomi ya Afrika-Dzoga.

src: The R2 172 359 000 is allocated to fight illicit mining, which continues to be a threat to the South African economy.
tgt: Mali yi averiwile SAPS, SANDF, Ndzawulo ya Xikaya, Border Management Agency.

src: The SAPS will use the funding to buy vehicles, helicopters, Nyalas and will deploy more 4 000 officers for 18 months.
tgt: SAPS yi ta tirhisa mali ku xava mimovha, swihahampfuka, Tilorhi no thola ku tlula 4 000 Vaofisiri tin’hweti ta Ku ceriwa ka migodi swi nga ri nawini na vugevenga byin’wana byo kunguhatiwa byi lahlekerisa Afrika-Dzonga tibiliyoni lembe na lembe no kavanyeta xiyimo xa hina xo va ndhawu ya vuvekisi.

src: Illegal mining and other organised crimes cost South Africa billions of rands each year and it affects our position as an investment destination.
tgt: Kungu ro Endla ku Cinca ka Eneji (JET-IP) Khabinete yi amukerile JET-IP, leyi nga ta letela ku cinca ka Afrika-Dzonga ku ya ka ikhonomi ya le hansi ya khabono hi ku tlakusa kumekelo ra eneji yo pfuxetiwa.

src: The Just Energy Transition Implementation Plan (JET-IP) Cabinet approved the JET-IP, which will guide South Africa’s transition to low carbon economy through the scaling up of renewable energy sources.
tgt: JET-IP yi endlile ku nghenelela ko tala loku Afrika-Dzonga yi ku lavaka na vuvekisi lebyi lavekaka ku tiko ri cinca ku ya ka khabono ya le hansi na ikhonomi yo tiyiseka ku cinca ka maxelo hi ku fambisana na National Determined Contributions loku andlariweke hi UKhabinete yi na mavonelo ya leswaku JET-IP yi kombisa ku tinyiketela ka Afrika-Dzonga eka ku cinca loku fambelanaka na laveko wa eneji wa tiko.

src: The JET-IP sets out a number of interventions South Africa needs and investments required for the country to transition to a low carbon and climate resilient economy in line with the National Determined Contributions presented to the UCabinet is of the view that the JET-IP demonstrates South Africa’s commitment to a just transition in line with the country’s energy needs.
tgt: JET-IP yi ta lawuriwa hi ku hlangana ka ku cinca eka sekitara ya eneji, ku katsa Mpumalanga Just Transition, New Energy Vehicles and Green Hydrogen, na tin’wana.

src: The JET-IP will be driven by a combination of reforms in the energy sector, including the Mpumalanga Just Transition, New Energy Vehicles and Green Hydrogen, among others.
tgt: Kungu ri ya emahlweni ri hlamula ku tiyimisela ka Afrika-Dzonga ehansi ka Paris Agreement na UN Framework Convention eka ku cinca ka maxelo na ku tiyimisela ka Kungu ra Rixaka ra Nhluvukiso (NDP).

src: The JET-IP will enable South Africa to gradually meet its carbon emissions reduction commitments while at the same time, it will ensure inclusive economic growth, energy security and employment.
tgt: JET-IP yi ta pfumelela Afrika-Dzonga ku fikelela ku tiyimisela hi switsongotsongo ku hunguta thyakiso wa moya loko hi nkarhi wun’we, yi tiyisisa ku kurisa ikhonomi hi ku angarhela, nhlayiso wa eneji na mitirho.

src: Draft National Public Transport Subsidy Policy Cabinet approved the gazetting of the draft National Public Transport Subsidy Policy for public comments.
tgt: Mpfapfarhuto wa Pholisi ya Mpfuno wa Vutleketli bya Mani na Mani Khabinete yi amukela gazete ya mpfapfarhuto wa Mpfapfarhuto wa Pholisi ya Mpfuno wa Vutleketli bya Mani na Mani leswaku vaakatiko va veka mavonelo.

src: The policy proposes that South Africa’s public transport funding should move from subsidising a particular mode of transport to a user-subsidy model.
tgt: Pholisi yi lava leswaku nkwama wa pfuneto vutleketli bya mani na mani eAfrika-Dzonga wu susiwa eka ku seketela muxaka wo karhi wa vutleketli wu ya seketela vatirhisi va vutleketli.

src: Government recognises that the transport sector is at the heart of the country’s development, with most households completely reliant on public transport for mobility.
tgt: Mfumo wu lemukile leswaku sekitara ya vutleketli i xivindzi xa nhluvukiso wa tiko, laha kwalomu ka mindyangu yo tala yi tshembeleke ngopfu eka vutleki bya mani na mani ku fambisiwa.

src: Biannual Medium Term Strategic Framework (MTSF) 2019-2024 performance progress reports Cabinet received and considered the MTSF biannual progress reports for the period 1 April 2023 to 30 September 2023.
tgt: Rimba ra Makungu ra Nkarhi wa le Xikarhi (MTSF) 2019-2024 xiviko xa matirhelo.

src: The reports form part of the consolidated government priorities towards the achievement of the NDP goals.
tgt: Swiviko i swiphemu swa hlangano wo rhangisa mimfumo eka ku fikelela swikongomelo swa NDXiviko xi languta eka nkombo wa swilo swa nkoka swa mfumo leswi nga kumiwa hi vufambisi bya vutsevu ku nga leswi: Xa Nkoka xo Sungula: Ku aka mfumo wa vuswikoti, matikhomelo na nhluvukiso

src: The reports focused on the seven priorities of government that were identified by the sixth administration namely: Priority One: Building a capable, ethical and developmental state
tgt: Xa Nkoka xa Vumbirhi: Vuswikoti bya Dyondzo na Rihanyo Xa Nkoka xa Vunarhu: Ku tiyisa mali ya mpfuno ku tshembeka na vukorhokeri bya Nkoka bya xiyimo xa le henhla Xa Nkoka xa Vumune: Ku ngenelela etindhawini, swidakanini na mimfumo ya miganga

src: Priority Five: Social Cohesion
tgt: Xa Nkoka xa Ntlhanu: Vuxaka bya Vaakatiko

src: Priority Six: Economic transformation and job creation Priority Seven: A better Africa and a better world.
tgt: Xa Nkoka xa Vutsevu: Ku Cinca Ikhonomi no tumbuluxa mitirho Xa Nkoka xa Vukombo: Afrika yo Antswa na misava yo antswa.

src: The Minister in The Presidency responsible for Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation will lead detailed briefings with the clusters on the Programme of Action.
tgt: Holobye ofisini ya Puresidente leyi langutanaka na Nkunguhato, Nkambisiso no Hlela yi ta rhangela mbhurisana na tlilasitara eka Phurogireme ya Xiendlo.

src: BILLS South African National Petroleum Company (SANPC) Bill Cabinet approved the publication of the SANPC Bill for public comments.
tgt: 20 Nawumbisi Nawumbisi wa Khaphani Petirolo ya Rixaka ra Afrika-Dzonga (SANPC) Khabinete yi pasisile ku kandziyisiwa ka Nawumbisi wa SANPC wu ya voniwa hi vanhu.

src: The Bill gives effect to the Cabinet decision to merge PetroSA, South African Gas Development Company (iGas) and the Strategic Fuel Fund.
tgt: Nawumbisi wu nyika matimba eka xiboho xa khabinete xo hlanganisa PetroSA, South African Gas Development Company (iGas) na Strategic Fuel Fund.

src: The Bill makes provisions for the establishment of a state-owned company that will ensure South Africa participates meaningfully in oil and gas development.
tgt: Nawumbisi wu nyika ku tumbuluxiwa ka khaphani leyi lawuriwaka hi mfumo leyi nga ta tiyisisa ku nghenelela ka Afrika-Dzonga yo vuyerisa eka ndlandlamuxo wa oyili na gasi.

src: It will also guarantee the country’s security of energy supply to support economic development and growth.
tgt: Yi ta tiyisisa nhlayiseko wa tiko wa mphakelo wa eneji ku seketela nhluvukiso no kula ka ikhonomi.

src: The SANPC will oversee strategic planning, coordination and governance of the country’s petroleum resources, and this will contribute to development and job creation.
tgt: SANPC yi ta langutisa tindlela ta makunguhatelo, ku lawula na vufambisi bya switirhisiwa swa tipetirolo bya tiko, naswona leswi swi ta engetela nhlukiso na endla mitirho.

src: Appointments All appointments are subject to the verification of qualifications and relevant clearance.
tgt: 21 Ku thoriwa Appointments Ku thoriwa hinkwako ku ya hi ku tiyisisiwa ka vuthwaseri na ku kamberiwa loku faneleke ka vuhlayiseki.

src: Reappointment of Dr Molefi Motuku as Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the Council for Mineral Technology (MINTEK) (reappointment) Appointment of Mr Siyabulela Koyo as CEO of Amatola Water Re-appointment of Ms Poppy Khoza as Managing Director of the South African Civil Aviation Authority (renewal of employment contract) Members of the Phongolo – Umzimkhulu Catchment Management Agency Board.
tgt: Ku thoriwa nakambe ka Dr Molefi Motuku tanihi Muofisirinkulu wa Xirho xa Huvonkulu (CEO) ya Council for Mineral Technology (MINTEK) (Ku thoriwa nakambe) Ku thoriwa ka Mr Siyabulela Koyo Tanihi CEO ya Amatola Water Ku thoriwa nakambe Ms Poppy Khoza as Murhangeri wa Vufambisi bya South African Civil Aviation Authority (Ku pfuxetiwa ka kotiraka) Swiro swa Phongolo – Umzimkhulu Catchment Management Agency Board.

src: Upcoming events 16 Days of Activism for No Violence against Women and Children (25 November to 10 December) This year marks the 25th Anniversary since South Africa initiated the 16 Days of Activism for No Violence against Women and Children campaign.
tgt: 22 Mitiro leyi taka Pfhumba ra Masiku ya 16 yo Lwisana na Madzolonga ehenhla ka Vavasati na Vana (25 Hukuri ku fika 10 N'wendzamhala) Leri i lembe ra vu 25 ra pfhumba kusukela loko Afrika-Dzonga ri simekile Pfhumba ra Masiku ya 16 yo Lwisana na Madzolonga ehenhla ka Vavasati na Vana.

src: The launch will be held in Mpumalanga at the Nsikazi Stadium, City of Mbombela under the theme: “Accelerating actions to end gender-based violence & femicide: leaving no one behind”.
tgt: Simeko wu ta khomeriwa eMpumalanga, eNsikazi Stadium, City of Mbombela ehansi ka nkongomelo: “Ku engetela migingiriko yo herisa madzolonga ku ya hi rimbewu no dlayiwa ka vavasati: ku nga siyiwi munhu endzhaku.” Nkongomelo wa Vumbirhi: “Ku hlayiseka ka vavasati ko kuma mati yo tenga: timfanelo ta ximunhu, ku vulavula hi swirhalanganyi vavasati va hlanganaka na swona eka hlayiseko wo kuma mati yo tenga na nkululo.

src: The sub-theme: “Safe access for women to clean water: a basic human right, addresses barriers women face in safely accessing water and sanitation.
tgt: Afrika- Dzonga na Yuniyono ya Comoros va ta endla swin’we Nhlengeletano ya Vunharhu ya Vavanuna mayelana na Matiktwelo ya Kahle eka Vurhangeri ku herisa Madzolonga ehenhla ka Vavasati na Vanhwanyana hi ti 27 na 28 Hukuri 2023 ePitori ehansi ka nkongomelo: Ku tiyisisa ku tiyimisela ku ya Nhlangano wa African Union mayelana na ku herisa Madzolonga ehenhla ka Vavasati na Vanhwanyana.”

src: Cabinet extended its congratulations and well-wishes to: ProfDire Tladi, formerly of the University of Pretoria, on his election by the UN as a judge of the International Court of Justice.
tgt: Khabinete yi hundzisele ku hoyozela na ku navelela leswinene eka: Phurofesa Dire Tladi, mutirhi wa Yunivhesiti ya Pitori, eka ku hlawuriwa hi UN tanihi muavanyisi wa Khoto ya Matiko ya Misava ya Vululami.

src: ProfTladi is a highly respected scholar, a skilled diplomat and is the first South African ever to be elected to the Court in its 78 year history, the second judge from the Southern African region and the second youngest judge ever to be selected to the court.
tgt: Phurofesa Tladi i xidyondzeki xo hlonipheka, muyimeri wa tiko wa tokoto naswona i mu Afrika-Dzonga wo sungula ku hlawuriwa eka Khoto eka malembe ya yona ya matimu ya 78, i muavanyisi wa vumbirhi kusuka eka matiko ya Afrika wa Vuxa-Dzonga naswona muavanyisi wa vumbirhi lowutsongo ku ta fika sweswi ku hlawuriwa eka khoto.

src: The AGSA for being appointed the external auditor of the UN Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization .
tgt: Ku thoriwa ka AGSA tanihi muoditi wa le handle wa Nhlangano wa UN wa Dyondzo, Xisatifiki na Ndhavuko.

src: This is a reaffirmation of the above-average international standing of South Africa’s institutions.
tgt: Leswi i ku tiyisisa ku yima kahle emisaveni ka miako ya Afrika-Dzonga.

src: Previously, the AGSA was an external auditor of the UN, more than 10 years ago.
tgt: Endzhaku, AGSA a yi ri muoditi wa le handle wa UN, ku hundza 10 wa malembe.

src: Mamelodi Sundowns for flying the flag high and making history by winning the Inaugural African Football League.
tgt: Mamelodi Sundowns eka ku hahisa mujeko henhla no endla matimu hi hlula eka African Football League yo sungula.

src: This triumph is another example of the unifying power of sport, which continues to foster nation-building and social cohesion.
tgt: Mhalamhala leyi I xikombiso xa ntwanano wa matima ya mitlango, lowu ya ka emahlweni ku aka rixaka na ntwanano wa vaaki.

src: Mamelodi Sundowns Ladies for becoming the CAF Women’s Champions League Final by beating Sporting Club Casablanca.
tgt: Vanhwanyana va Mamelodi Sundowns ku fikelela rhengu ro hetelela ra CAF Women’s Champions League hi ku hlula Sporting Club Casablanca.

src: The Proteas for demonstrating resilience and fighting spirit in their defeat against Australia in the Cricket World Cup semi-finals and congratulate Australia for winning the ICC 2023 World Cup.
tgt: Proteas hi ku kombisa ku tiyisela na moya wo lwa eku hluriweni ka vona hi Australia eka semi- fayinali ta Khapu ya Misava ya Cricket no hoyozela Australia ku va va hlurile eka Khapu ya Misava ya ICC 2023.

src: Legendary actor and playwright Dr John Kani, who has been awarded an honorary Officer of the Most Excellent Order of the British Empire (OBE) in recognition for his services to drama.
tgt: Mutlangi tlhelo mutsari wa ntokoto Dokodela John Kani, loyi a yikiweke Officer of the Most Excellent Order of the British Empire (OBE) ku ri ndlela tlangela ntirho wa yena eka ntlangu.

src: An OBE is a British chivalric order which recognises one for making great impact in their line of work.
tgt: OBE i British chivalric order leyi tekelaka nhlokweni munhu loyi tisaka ku cinca ku kulu eka tirho wa vona.

src: Minister of Higher Education, Science and Innovation, Dr Blade Nzimande, who has been awarded an honorary professorship by the Beijing Jiaotong University in China.
tgt: Holobye wa Dyondzo ya le Henhla, Sayense na Nkambisiso Dokodela Blade Nzimande, loyi a nyikiweke xiximo wa vuphurofesa hi yunivhesiti ya Beijing Jiaotong eChina.

src: This is in recognition of his contributions to education, and is a symbol of strengthening ties between South Africa and China.
tgt: Leswi i ku tekela enhlokweni xiave xa yena eka dyondzo, na xikombiso xo tiyisa vuxaka exikarhi ka Afrika-Dzonga na China.

src: Dr Kogie Naidoo, who was awarded the prestigious Outstanding Female Scientist Prize presented by the European and Developing Countries Clinical Trials Partnership - a research programme of the European Union.
tgt: Dokodela Kogie Naidoo loyi a nyikiweke Outstanding Female Scientist Prize leyi andlariweke hi European and Developing Countries Clinical Trials Partnership – Phurogireme ya ndzavisiso wa European Union.

src: South Africa’s InvestSA, a branch of the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic) that won a UN Investment Promotion Award at the 8th World Investment Forum, for promoting and facilitating a large energy project that includes foreign investment for the construction of the country's largest renewable energy project, expected to provide clean energy to 200 000 households.
tgt: InvestSA ya Afrika-Dzonga, leyi nga rhavi ra Ndzawulo ya Mabindzu, Vumaki na Mphikizano (the dtic) leyi wineke sagwati ra UN Investment Promotion eka 8th World Investment Forum hi ku tlakusa no languta phurojeke yikulu ya eneji leyi katsaka va vekisi va vahlapfa eka ku akiwa ka phurojeke yikulu ya tiko ya eneji, leyi languteriweke ku nyika 200 000 mindyangu eneji yo basa.

src: South Africa was ranked in first place in the GBS World Competitiveness Index, for its support for call centres in the category of ‘Global Customer Lifecycle Management’ and ranked second in the Global Customer Service and Support Services category.
tgt: Afrika-Dzonga vekiwile eka xiyimo xo sungula eka mphikizano wa Misava wa GBS Index, ku va yi seketerile tisentara ta tiqingho eka xiyenge xa ‘Global Customer Lifecycle Management’ no vekiwa eka xiyimoxa vumbirhi eka xiyenge xa Global Customer Service and Support Services.

src: Condolences Cabinet expressed condolences to the family and friends of: South African music icon Marc Rantseli, who was part of the musical duo Marc Alex which he co-founded with his brother Alex Rantseli.
tgt: Ku chavelela condolences Khabinete yi kombisile ku chavelela eka ndyangu na vanghana va: Muyimbeleri wo tiveka wa Afrika-Dzonga Marc Rantseli, loyi a ri xirho xa ntlawa wa Marc Alex lowu a wu tumbuluxeka na buti wa yena Alex Rantseli.

src: Legendary former sports journalist and news editor Sello Rabothata.
tgt: Khale ka nhenha yo teka mahungu ya mitlangu no hlela mahungu Sello Rabothata.

src: He is known for his love of football, and formed part of the team that helped coin the name Bafana-Bafana for South Africa’s National Soccer Team.
tgt: U tiveka hi rirhandzu ra yena ra bolo, no va xirho xa ntlawa lowu pfuneke ku tumbuluxa vito ra Bafana-Bafana ra Xipano xa Bolo ya Milenge ya Afrika-Dzonga.

src: Much-loved radio personality Irvin Sihlophe, who anchored and produced sports shows on SABC’s Ukhozi FA Palestine but a Head of the Gift of the Givers Gaza office, Ahmed Abbasi, who was killed in the ongoing Israel-Hamas war.
tgt: Muhaxi wo rhandzeka wa Xiyanimoya Irvin Sihlophe, loyi a haxa no humelerisa nongonoko wa mitlangu eka SABC’s Ukhozi FMupalesitina kambe Nhloko ya Gift of the Givers Gaza office, Ahmed Abbasi, loyi a dlayiweke enga yimpi ya Israel-Hamas leyi ya ka emahlweni.

src: .1 Cabinet welcomed the 2024 National Budget, which demonstrated the resolute commitment by government to consistently manage the country’s economy and take tough decisions necessary to balance the deficit while promoting economic growth.
tgt: Timhaka leti nga eka Mbango Ikhonomi Mbulavulo wa Bajete ya Tiko Khabinete yi amukela Bajete ya Tiko ya 2024, leyi yi kombaka ku tiyimisela ka mfumo k uya emahlweni wu lawula ikhonomi ya tiko na ku teka swiboho swo tika leswi lavekaka eka ringanisa nkayivelo loko yi r ikarhi yi hluvukiso ku kula ka ikhonomi.

src: .2 The National Budget continues to drive critical priorities and support for the most vulnerable of our nation.
tgt: Bajete ya Tiko yi ya emahlweni ku fambisa swilaveko swa nkoka na nseketelo wa lava pfumalaka va tiko ra hina.

src: It provides social assistance to improve the living conditions of poor, vulnerable and underprivileged South Africans.
tgt: Yi nyika nseketelo eka vaaki ku antswisa xiyimo xa rihanyo eka swixiwana, lava nga eka nxungeto na lava nga eka xiyimo xaansi eAfrika-Dzonga.

src: These include unemployed South Africans, and orphaned and vulnerable children living in child- headed households.
tgt: Leswi swi katsa lava nga tirhiki va le Afrika-Dzonda, na swisiwana na vana lava nga eka nxungeto lava va tshamaka emakaya lama rhangeleke hi vana.

src: .3 The consolidation and tabling of the 2024 National Budget is an important part of South Africa’s open and accountable system of democracy.
tgt: Ku katsakanya na ku veka etafuleni Bajete ya Tiko ya 2024 i xiphemu xa nkoka xa matirhelo ya demokirasi ya Afrika-Dzonga leyo pfuleka na vutihlamuleri.

src: Cabinet is confident that the National Budget allocations will translate into economic gains that rebuild our economic standing.
tgt: Khabinete yi na ntshembo wa leswaku mikavelo ya Bajete ya Tiko yi ta va na mimbuyelo eka ikhonomi leyi nga ta aka nakambe xiyimo xa ikhonomi ya hina.

src: .1 Cabinet welcomed the first-of-its-kind public-private partnership agreement between Sasol and Transnet Freight Rail to improve the reliability of rail transport.
tgt: Ntirhisano wa Vatiyimeri-Mfumo Khabinete yi amukela ntwanano wa ntirhisano wa vatiyimeri-mfumo wa muxaka wa wona exikarhi ka Sasol na Transnet Freight Rail ku antswisa ku tshemebela eka vutleketli bya le xiporweni.

src: .2 Under a five-year agreement, Transnet Freight Rail will use its fleet of 128 ammonia tankers to deliver ammonia from Sasol facilities to customer and in return Sasol will fund the maintenance and repair programme of the fleet.
tgt: Ehansi ka ntwanano wa ntlhanu wa malembe, Transnet Freight Rail yi ta tirhisa swifambo swa yona swa 128 swa tithenkara ta amoniya ku tleketla amoniya ku suka eka switirhisiwa swa Sasol ku ya eka vaxavi naswona hi ku hlamula, Sasol yi ta hakela nongonoko wo hlayisa na ku lunghisa swifambo.

src: .3 The partnership advances work on the country’s Freight Logistics Roadmap to turn around the sector.
tgt: Vutirhisani byi yisa emahlweni ntirho wa tiko wa Freight Logistics Roadmap ku antswisa xiyenge lexi.

src: This partnership demonstrates how together we can overcome our pressing challenges.
tgt: Vutirhisano lebyi byi kombisa hilaha loko hi tirhisana hi nga hlulaka hakona swiphiqo leswo tika.

src: .1 Statistics South Africa’s recent QLFS that showed a slight rise in the country’s unemployment rate in the fourth quarter of 2023 to 32.1% from 31.9% in the third quarter, motivates us as government to redouble our efforts to draw more people into work opportunities.
tgt: Mbalango wa Kotara wa Swa Mitirho (QLFS) QLFS wa sweswi wa Tinhlayonhlayo ta Afrika-Dzonga wu komba ku tlakuka kutsongo ka ku pfumaleka ka mitirho eka kotara ya vumune ya 2023 ku ya eka 32.1% ku suka eka 31,9% eka kotara ya vunharhu, ya hi hlohlotela tanihi mfumo ku mbirhihata matshalathsala ya hina ku nghenisa vanhu vo tala eka swivandla swa mitirho.

src: .2 While our economy continues to create jobs, it is not at the level that government aims to achieve in order to address the challenge of unemployment.
tgt: Loko ikhonomi ya hina yi ya emahlweni ku vanga mitirho, a swi le ka mpimo lowu mfumo wu swi bohiseke xiswona ku swi fikelela ku kuma tinhlamulo ta swiphiqo swo pfumaleka ka mitirho.

src: The QLFS showed that the informal sector employment increased by 124 000, finance by 128 000 jobs,
tgt: QLFS yi komba leswaku xiyenge xa mitirho leyi ng ariki ya ximfumo swi engeterile hi 124 000, swa timali hi 128 000, vutleketli hi 57 000, swa migodi hi 37 000 ya mitirho naswona vatirhi va le makaya hi mitirho ya 18 000.

src: .3 Cabinet called on all sectors to support the Economic Reconstruction and Recovery Plan, which is helping to provide work and livelihood opportunities to millions of South Africans.
tgt: Khabinete yi rhamba swiyenge hinkwaswo ku seketela pfhumba ra Economic Reconstruction and Recovery Plan, leri ri pfunaka ku nyika swivandlanene swa mitirho na ku tihanyisa ka Maafrika-Dzonga.

src: 20th Anniversary of Expanded Public Works Programme (EPWP)
tgt: Ntlangelo wa vu20 wa Phurogireme ya Ndlandlamuxo wa Swa Mitirho (EPWP) Lembe ra 2024 ri fungha 20 wa malembe w aku va kona ka EPWP, leyi yi yimelaka swin’wana swa switori swa ku humelela ka Afrika-Dzonga eka nongonoko wa rona wa mohakelo wa mitirho eka vanhu naswona hi wun’wana wa migingiriko leyikulu yo susa vusweti.

src: .1 The year 2024 marks 20 years of the existence of the EPWP, which represents one of South Africa’s success stories of mass public employment programmes and is by far one of the largest poverty alleviation initiatives.
tgt: Khabinete yi kumile nkatsakanyo eka ku simeka na ku humelela ka EPWP, nongonoko lowukulu wa mfumo lowu nyikeke mamiliyoni ya swivadlanene swa mitirho eka vapfumari va mitirho va Afrika-Dzonga ku suka loko wu sungurile.

src: .2 Cabinet received a briefing on the implementation and achievements of the EPWP, a flagship government programme that has provided millions of work opportunities to unemployed South Africans since its inception.
tgt: EPWP eka malembe ya 20 lama nga hundza wu tumbuluxile 14 wa mamiliyoni ya swivandla swa mitirho, leswi swi wu endlaka wu va nongonoko wa mitnirho lowukulu lowu ya ka emahlweni emisaveni.

src: This milestone was achieved through continuous partnerships with the private sector and civil society.
tgt: Ntirho lowukulu wu fikeleriwile hikwalaho ka ntirhisano lowu yaka emahlweni na xiyenge lexi tiyimelaka na mihlangano ya vaaki.

src: These work opportunities have contributed to skills development for the participants as they were created under a range of EPWP projects in the tourism, agriculture, infrastructure, social projects and projects led by women.
tgt: Swivandla swa mitirho leswi swi hoxile xandla eka nhluvukiso wa vuswioti eka vatekaxiave tanihiloko yi tumbuluxiwa ehansi ka tipurojeke ta EPWP eka swa vupfhumba, vurimi, switirhisiwa, tipurojeke ta vanhu na tipurojeke leti rhangeleke hi vamanana.

src: .4 Cabinet was informed that 4 609 000 work opportunities were created during Phase 4 medium term of the EPWP, which covers the period 2019/2020 – 2022/23.
tgt: Khabinete yi byeriwile leswaku 4 609 000 wa swivandla swa mitirho swi tumbuluxiwile hi Phase 4 ya kotara ya le xikarhi ya EPWP, leyi katsaka nkarhi wa 2019/2020 – 2022/23.

src: This figure represents a 92% achievement against the target set by the Sixth Administration to create five million work opportunities.
tgt: Nhlayo leyi yi yimela ku humelela ka 92% ku hundza mpimo lowu a wu vekiwile hi Vulawuri bya Vutsevu ku tumbuluxa ntlhanu wa mamiliyoni ya s wivandla swa mitirho.

src: Plans are in place to achieve the remaining 390 973 work opportunities by March 2024.
tgt: Makungu ya le ndleleni ku fikelela 390 973 wa swivandla swa mitirho leswi saleke ku nga si fika Nyenyuanyani 2024.

src: .5 Of the 4 609 000 work opportunities, the top three provinces where most work opportunities have been created are KwaZulu-Natal, which accounts for 1 064 000 opportunities (23%), followed by the
tgt: Eka swivandla swa mitirho swa 4 609 000, swifundzhankulu swinharhu leswi nga ehenhla laha swivandla swa intirho swi tumbuluxiweke kona i KwaZulu-Natal, leyi tihlamuleleka hi 1 064 000 wa swivandla (23%), yi landzela hi Kapavuxa, hi 903 789 (20%) na Kapa-Vupeladyambu hi 508 954 (11%).

src: .6 Although most of these opportunities are short term to medium term, some have resulted in permanent employment.
tgt: Hambiloko swivandla leswi swi ri swa xinkadyana ku fika eka nkarhinyana, swin’wana swi helele eka mitirho ya ntiyiso.

src: Figures also indicate that more than 20% of participants obtained employment outside the EPW.7 Many past EPWP participants have successfully completed diplomas in fields such as professional cookery and some are permanently employed in the hospitality industry.
tgt: Tinhlayo ti tlhela ti hi komba leswaku ku tlula 20% wa vatekaxiave va kumile mitirho ehandle ka EPWVatekaxiave vo tala eka EPWP va kumile tidipiloma eka swiyenge swo tanihi vasweki va ntokoto naswona van’wana va thoriwile swa nkarhikunkwawo eka xiyenge xa vupfhumba.

src: In addition to work opportunities, the EPWP also contributes much more in terms of service delivery, and improvements of amenities in communities and a better quality of life.
tgt: Ku engetela eka swivandla swa mitirho, EPWP nakambe yi hoxa xandla hi xitalo eka mphakelo wa vukorhokeri, na ku antswisa swijtirhisiwa emigangeni na ku antswisa vujtomi buya vanhu.

src: .8 Over R52 billion has been transferred to the EPWP participants as wages for work done in Phase I.9 In addition, over 600 businesses were established through the programme.
tgt: Ku tlula R52 wa mabiliyoni yi nyikiwile vatekaxiave eka EPWP tanihi miholo ya ntirho lowu endliweke hi Phase IKu engetela, ku tlula 600 wa mabindzu ya simekiwile hi nongonoko lowu.

src: 2 Governance matters 2024 General Elections
tgt: Timhaka ta Mfumo Mihlawulo ya Mani na Mani ya 2024 Khabinete yi amukela xitiviso xa Puresidente Cyril Ramaphosa xa leswaku 29 Mudyaxihi 2024 i siku ra Mihlawulo ya Mani na Mani, hi ku landza ku tihlanganisa ka yena na Khomixini ya Nhlawulo ya Afrika-Dzonga na Tiphirimiya ta kaye wa swifundzhankulu mayelana na ku tilulamisela ka swona eka mihlawulo ya tiko na ya swifundzhankulu.

src: .2 The Cabinet called on everyone, especially the youth, to exercise their right to vote.
tgt: Khabinete yi rhamba hinkwavo, ngopfungopfu vantshwa, ku tirhisa mfanelo ya vona yo vhota.

src: Years of untold sacrifice and struggle for our freedom culminated in the right to vote for the majority of South Africans in 1994.
tgt: Malembe lamotala yo titsona na ku lwela ntshuxeko swi hetelele eka mfanelo yo vhota eka lavo tala va Afrika-Dzonga hi 1994.

src: Our struggle for freedom secured the right for every South African to be active participants in our democratic system.
tgt: Ku lwela ka hina ntshuxeko swi vuyerisile mfanelo ya Muafrika-Dzonga un’wana na un’wana ku teka xiave hi xiviri eka mafambiselo ya xidemokirasi.

src: .3 This year’s elections coincide with the celebration of 30 Years of Freedom, which is a significant milestone for South Africa as it provides us with the opportunity to reflect on our successes and also look for solutions to address our surmountable challenges.
tgt: Mihlawulo ya lembe leri yi kotlana na ntlangelo wa 30 wa Malembe ya Ntshuxeko, leswi swi nga goza lerikulu eka Afrika-Dzonga tanihilaha swi hi nyikaka nkarhi wo languta endzhaku eka ku humelela ka hina na ku lava swintshuxo ku hlamula swiphiqo swa hina leswo tala.

src: .1 Cabinet noted President Ramaphosa’s meeting on Friday, 23 February 2024 with the Durban Chamber of Commerce and Industry to discuss various initiatives led by national government to assist the eThekwini Metropolitan Municipality to address the current water, electricity and infrastructure challenges.
tgt: Ntlawa wo Tirha wa eThekwini wa le ka Puresidente Khabinete yi tekela enhlokweni nhlangano wa Puresidente Cyril Ramaphosa hi avuntlahnu, 23 Nyenyanyana 2024 na Nhlangano wa Mabindzu wa Durban na Vumaki ku kanela hi matshalatshala ya mfumo ku pfuna eThekwini Metropolitan Municipality ku lulamisa swiphiqo leswi nga kona sweswi swa mati, gezi na switirhisiwa.

src: .2 The President also established the Presidential eThekwini Working Group to accelerate the speedy resolution of issues affecting the eThekwini Metropolitan Municipality.
tgt: Nakambe Puresidente u simekile Ntlawa wo Tirha wa eThekwini wa le ka Puresidente ku hatlisisa ku kuma swintshuxo swa swiphiqo leswi khumbaka eThekwini Metropolitan Municipality.

src: The group – comprising Ministers, and eThekwini Metropolitan Municipality and business officials – will regularly present progress reports to the President 14th Policy Dialogue Forum of the International Task Force on Teachers for Education
tgt: Ntlawa – lowu vumbeke hi Vaholobye, na swirho swa mabindzu swa eThekwini Metropolitan Municipality – hi mikarhi va ta andlala swiviko swo leswi yaka emahlweni eka Puresidente.

src: .1 Cabinet noted the country’s successful hosting of the 14th PDF of the International Task Force on Teachers for Education in Sandton, Johannesburg on Monday, 26 February 2024.
tgt: Foramu ya vu14 ya N’wangulano wa Pholisi (PDF) ya Migingiriko ya Matiko ya Tinxakanxaka eka Dyondzo ya Vadyondzisi Khabinete yi tekela enhlokweni ku humelela eka ku rhurhela Foramu ya vu14 ya N’wangulano wa Pholisi ya Migingiriko ya Matiko ya Tinxakanxaka eka Dyondzo ya Vadyondzisi eSandton, eJoni hi Musumbhuluko, 26 Nyenyanyana 2024.

src: It brought together education stakeholders from across the globe to foster advocacy, knowledge exchange and the monitoring of progress towards Sustainable Development Goal 4 on quality education.
tgt: Swi hlengeletile vatekaxiave eka dyondzo va tinxakaxaka ta misava ku hlohlotela nseketelo, ku avelana vutivi na ku landzelerisa Nhluvukiso wa Xikongomelo xa 4 xa dyondzo ya nkoka.

src: .2 The Policy Dialogue Forum released a High-Level Panel Report on the Teaching Profssion and also launched the Global Report on teacher shortages.3 Crime Combating Cabinet commends the South African Police Service for their tireless work, which has led to the arrest of seven persons in connection with the murder of Kiernan 'AKA' Forbes and his friend Tebello 'Tibs' Motsoane.
tgt: PDF yi humesile xiviko xa High-Level Panel Report on the Teaching Profession na ku simeka Xiviko xa Misava eka nkayivelo wa vadyondzisi.

src: Two of the suspects were arrested in Eswatini and are still to be extradited to the country.
tgt: Ku sivela vugevenga Khabinete yi hoyozela Ndzawulo ya Maphorisa ya Afrika-Dzonga eka ntirho wa vona lowo tsandza ku karhala, lowu ng ava fikisa eka ku khoma vanhu va nkombo hi mayelana na ku dlaya ka Kiernan 'AKA' Forbes na munghana wa yena Tebello ‘Tibz’ Motsoane.

src: The arrests are as result of months of painstaking police work.
tgt: Ku khomiwa loku swi hikwalaho ka ntirho lowo vava swinene wa maphorisa.

src: The suspects arrested included a coordinator, shooters, spotter and person who hired the vehicle and firearms.
tgt: Vaehlekeleriwa va katsa muhlanganisi, vabalesi, tinhlori, na munhu loyi a nga lomba movha na swibalesa.

src: .1 Cabinet appreciated the progress made at the 37th AU Summit held in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia on 17 and 18 February 2024, which outlined Africa's priorities for 2024 and beyond.
tgt: Vuxaka bya Matiko ya Tinxakaxaka Nhlengeletano ya vu37 ya Nhlangano wa Matiko ya Afrika Khabinete yi khensa nhluvuko lowu endliweke eka Nhlengeletano ya AU ya vu37 leyi veke eAddis Ababa, Ethiopia hi 17 na 18 Nyenyanyana 2024, leyi a yi andlala swilaveko swa Afrika swa 2024 na ku ya emhahlweni.

src: President Ramaphosa joined other African leaders in discussing key continental priorities including peace and security, climate change, economic development and Africa’s role in the wider global multilateral context.
tgt: Puresidente Ramaphosa u tikatsile na swirho swin’wana swa varhangeri va Afrika eka ku kanela swilavekonkulu swa tikonkulu leswi katsaka ku rhula na nsirhelelo, ku cinca ka tinguva, nhluvukiso wa ikhonomi na ntirho wa Afrika eka swiyimo swa misava hi ku angarhela.

src: .2 The summit adopted the Second 10-Year Implementation Plan of Agenda 2063, which will see the acceleration of flagship projects such as the African Continental Free Trade Area, in which South Africa is playing a leading role.
tgt: Nhlengeletano yi tiyisisile Lembe ra vumbirhi ra Ku Simekiwa ka Kungu ra Agendza 2063 ra 10- wa Malembe, leswi swi nga ta endla ku hatlisisiwa ka tipurojeke letikulu to tanihi African Continental Free Trade Area, laha Afrika-Dzonga ri tekaka xiave xo rhangela.

src: .3 President Ramaphosa also presented a report on the continent’s response to the Coronavirus Disease (COVID-19) pandemic and the state of readiness against future health threats, in his capacity as the Champion of the AU’s COVID-19 response.
tgt: Puresidente Ramaphosa nakambe u andlarile xiviko xa tikonkulu xa ku hlamulana na ntungu wa Mavabyi ya Khorona (COVID-19) na xiyimo xo tiyimisela eka mixungeto ya rihanyo leyi ya ha taka, tanihi xiyimo xa yena xa Nhenha ya AU eka COVID-19.

src: The summit also emphasised the importance of socio-economic recovery post COVID-19, and lessons from the pandemic preparedness and response and continental security.
tgt: Nhlengeletano nakambe yi tiyisisile nkoka wa ikhonomi ya vanhu endzhaku ka ku sawuta eka COVID-19, na tidyondzo to huma eka ntungu ku tiyimisela na tinhlamulo, na nsirhelelo wa tikonkulu.

src: .4 The President called on African leaders to continue improving the levels of alertness of their countries against future pandemics and urged for the adoption of a strong Common Africa Position on Pandemic Preparedness and Response.
tgt: Puresidente u hlohlotela varhangeri va Afrika ku ya emahlweni va antswisa swiyimo swa switsunfdzuxo eka matiko ya vona eka mintungu leyi ya ha taka na ku hlohlotela ku tekela enhlokweni loku tiyeke ka Xiyimo Xin’we xa Afrika eka ku Tilulamisela na ku Angula eka Mintungu.

src: South Africa’s hosting of the Group of Twenty (G20) and Presidency in 2025
tgt: Ku rhurhela ka Afrika-Dzonga Ntlawa wa Matiko ya Makumembirhi (G20) na Hofisi ya Puresidente hi 2025 Khabinete yi amukerile na ku xopaxopa xiviko eka ku tilulamisela ka Afrika-Dzonga eka ku rhurhela Nhlengeletano ya G20 hi 2025 xikan’we na ku teka ka Ndzawulo ya Puresidente.

src: .1 Cabinet received and considered a report on the preparations for South Africa’s hosting of the G20 Summit in 2025 as well as taking over the Presidency.
tgt: Lexi i xiendleko lexikulu xa Afrika-Dzonga tanihiloko ri ta va tikor o sungula ra Afrika ku rhurhela nhlengeletano yo tani ehandle ka leswaku yi hlawulekile hikwalaho ka tinhlayo leti languteriwaka kambe nakambe na hi nkoka lowukulu lowu yi languteriwaka ku wu endla.

src: This is a momentous event for South Africa as it will be the first country in Africa to host such a gathering not only unique because of the anticipated numbers but also of the enduring impact it is envisaged to make.
tgt: Khabinete yina ku tshemba leswaku Afrika-Dzonga ri ta humelerisa Nhlengeletano ya G20, tanihiloko ri swi endlile hi swiendleko leswikulu swo tanihi hi Nhlengeletano ya Brazil, Russia, India, China na Afrika-Dzonga (BRICS) na African Growth and Opportunity Act Forum.

src: .2 Cabinet is confident that South Africa will deliver a successful G20 Summit, as it has done with previous major events such as the Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa Summit and the African Growth and Opportunity Act Forum.
tgt: G20 hi Ndzawulo ya Puresidente yi nyka Afrika-Dzonga nkarhi wo tiyisisa ku navela ka rona ka timakete leti ta ha kulaka.

src: The G20 Presidency presents South Africa with an opportunity to champion the aspirations of emerging markets.
tgt: Tanihiloko ri rhurhela G20, ku teka xiave ka Afrika-Dzonga eka foramu swi ta ya emahlweni ku leteriwa hi ku tiyimisela ka tiko ku yisa emahlweni ku navela ka tiko xikan’we na lokuya ka tikonkulu ra Afrika.

src: .3 As it hosts the G20, South Africa’s participation in the forum will continue to be guided by the country’s commitment to advance national interests as well as those of the African continent.
tgt: Swiboho swa Khabinete Ku rhurhela nhlengeletano ya lembe na lembe ya Vukaye ya Bangi Yintshwa ya Nhluvukiso (NDB) Khabinete yi xopaxopile na ku pfumelela ku rhurheriwa ka nhlengeletano ya lembe na lembe ya NDB eAfrika-Dzonga hi Khotavuxika 2024.

src: Cabinet decisions Hosting of the Ninth annual meeting of the New Development Bank (NDB) Cabinet considered and approved the hosting of the annual meeting of the NDB in South African in South African in June 2024.
tgt: Ku hundzile 10 ra malembe ku suka loko matiko ya BRICS ma sayinile Atikili ya Ntwanano wa NDB eka Nhlengeletano ya BRICS ya vu6 eFortaleza, Brazil hi 15 na 16 July 2014.

src: So far, South Africa has contributed R25 billion towards the bank’s paid in Capital.
tgt: Ku fika sweswi, Afrika-Dzonga ri hoxile R25 wa mabiliyoni eka bangi ku hakela Mali.

src: South Africa is looking forward to host the meeting on NDB and commits to working hand in hand with the bank and its member countries to achieve sustainable development and create a better the African continent.
tgt: Afrika-Dzonga ri lamgutela ku rhurhela nhlengeletano ya NDB naswona ri tiyimiserile ku tirhisana na bangi xikan’we na swirho swa yona swa matiko ku fikelela nhluvukiso lowu tiyeke na ku tumbuluxa Afrika lero antswa.

src: Strategy for the Employment of Social Service Profssionals (SSPs) Cabinet approved the Strategy for the Employment of SSPs as part of increasing the human resource capacity of government, non- governmental organisations and the private sector to proactively respond to social ills that are facing the country.
tgt: Qhinga ra ku Thoriwa ka Vatokoti va Vukorhokeri bya Vanhu (SSPs) Khabinete yi amukerile Qhinga ra ku Thoriwa ka SSPs tanihi xiphemu xo engetela vuswikoti bya vatirhi eka mfumo, mihlangano leyi nga riki ya mfumo na swiyenge leswi tiyimeleke ku angula eka vubihi lebyi kongomaneke na tiko.

src: The strategy is a collective commitment to building a social service sector that is responsive to the needs of our communities and overcome social ills such as crime, gender-based violence and femicide, teenage pregnancies, bullying, child-headed households, mental health and substance abuse.
tgt: Qhinga leri i ku tiyimisela ka nhlanganelo ku aka xiyenge xa vukorhokeri bya vaaki lexi xi angulaka vukorhokeri bya le migangeni ya hina na ku hlula vubihi eka vaaki byo tanihi vugevenga, madzolonga ya le mindyangwini na xihlawuhlawu hi rimbewu, ku biha emirimi ka vantshwa, vunhenha, mindyangu leyi rhangeriwaka hi vana, mavabyi ya miehleketo na ku tirhisiwa ka swidzidziharisi.

src: The strategy is also aimed at laying the foundation for a socially inclusive and resilient future and a caring society.
tgt: Nakambe qhinga ri kongomisiwile eka ku aka masungulo ku katsa vaaki na vumundbzuku lebyi tiyeke na vutshamo lebyi hlayisaka.

src: Green Paper on Comprehensive Social Security Cabinet considered and approved the publication and call for public comments on the revised Green Paper on Comprehensive Social Security for the country.
tgt: Phepha ra Rihlaza eka Nkatsakanyo wa Nsirhelelo wa Vanhu Khabinete yi xopaxopile na ku nyika mpfumelelo eka ku hangalasiwa na ku kombela mavonelo ya vanhu eka Phepha ra Rihlaza eka Nkatsakanyo wa Nsirhelelo wa Vanhu etikweni.

src: The paper aims to introduce a mandatory social security pension system that provides retirement, disability and death benefits to all workers.
tgt: Phepha leri ri na xikongomelo xo sungula penxeni ya nsirhelelo wa vaaki lowu nyikaka mbuyelo eka ku tshika ntirho, vutsoniwa na mafu eka vatirhi hinkwavo.

src: Low- income earners would have their contributions subsidised in line with existing provisions.
tgt: Lava va holaka mali ya le hansi tihakelo ta vona ti ta va na nseketelo ku ya hi swilaveko leswi nga kona.

src: The paper further proposes the harmonisation of the tax treatment of older persons in the tax and social grant system to address the unequal treatment of older persons in the two regimes.
tgt: Phepha ri ya emahlweni ri ringanyeta ku katsakanyiwa ka xibalo xa vadyuhari eka xibalo na maendlelo ya midende ku angula eka maendlelo ya nkandzingano eka vadyuhari eka swiyenge swimbirhi.

src: In addition, the paper also seeks to propose institutional reforms to promote coherence in social security policy making for administrative efficiency, improved service delivery and ensure effective regulation, governance and oversight across all social security arrangements.
tgt: Ku engetela, phepha ri lava ku pimanyeta ku cinca eka mihlangano ku kurisa mfambelano wa pholisi ya nsirhelelo wa vaaki leswaku ku va na mafambiselo ya kahle, mphakeo wa vukorhokeri lebyi antswaka na ku tiyisisa malawulelo lamanene, mafumelo na ku landzelerisa eka mintwanano hinkwayo ya nsirhelelo wa vaaki.

src: Appointments
tgt: Ku thoriwa

src: All appointments are subject to the verification of qualifications and relevant security clearances.
tgt: Ku thoriwa hinkwako ku ta lawula hi ntiyisiso wa tidyondzo na vubasisi lebyi faneleke.

src: Appointment of Mr Snike Thulani Sibuyi as Secretary for Police Service at the Department of Civil Secretariat for Police Service.
tgt: Ku thoriwa ka Tatana Snike Thulani Sibuyi tanihi Matsalani wa Ndzawulo ya Maphorisa eka Ndzawulo ya Vutsalani Ku thoriwa ka Tatana Xolile Sizani hi Mulawurinkulu (CEO) wa PetroSKu thoriwa ka Manana Nombulelo Guliwe tanihi Mulawurinkulu wa swa Vupfumba eAfrika-Dzonga.

src: Appointment of Mr Xolile Sizani as the Chief Executive Officer of Petro SAppointment of Ms Nombulelo Guliwe as CEO of South African Tourism Extension of contract for Ms Totsie Memela-Khambula as the Chief Executive Officer of the South African Social Security Agency.
tgt: Ku engeteriwa ka kontiraka ya Manana Totsie Memela-Khambula tanihi CEO ya Xiyenge xa Nsirhelelo wa Vaaki xa Afrika-Dzonga.

src: Appointment of the CEO of the Municipal Infrastructure Support Agency
tgt: Ku thoiwa ka Manana Mapatane Elizabeth Kgomo tanihi CEO ya Xiyenge xa Nseketelo wa Switirhisiwa swa Timasipala.

src: Re-appointment to the Board of Central Energy Fund (CEF) and appointment as chairperson Ms Ayanda Noah.
tgt: Ku thoriwanakambe eka Bodo ya Nkwama wa le Xikarhi wa Eneji (CEF) na ku thoriwa ka Manana Ayanda Noah tanihi Mutshamaxitulu.

src: Appointment of members of the South Africa Tourism Board: Ms Makhosazana Khanyile (Chairperson) Adv.
tgt: Ku thoriwa ka swirho swa Bodo ya Vupfumba ya Afrika-Dzonga: Ms Makhosazana Khanyile (Mutshamaxitulu) Adv Lizelle Dominique Jordaan (Xandla xa Mutshamaxitulu) Dr Gregory J Davids Tatana Ikaneng Ephraim Pilane Prof Motlhago Stella Bvuma Manana Nqabomzi Haya Tatana Rajesh Mahabeer Tatana Ayanda V Mazibuko Manana Maija de Rijk-Uys Dr Mzolisi Michael Toni na Manana Uveshnee Pillay tanihi muyimeri wa Ndzawulo ya Ndzawulo ya Vupfhumba.

src: Lizelle Dominique Jordaan (Deputy Chairperson) Dr Gregory Davids Mr Ikaneng Ephraim Pilane ProfMotlhago Stella Bavuma Ns Nqabomzi Haya Mr Rajesh Mahabeer Mr Ayanda Mazibuko Ms Maija de Rijk-Uys Dr Mzolisi Michael Toni and Ms Uveshnee Pillay as the Department representative Appointment of the Chairperson and Deputy Chairperson of the Board of Trustees of the Independent Development Trust: Adv Kwazikwenkosi Mshengu (Chairperson) and Ms Karabo Siyila (Deputy Chairperson).
tgt: Ku thoriwa ka Mutshamaxitulu na Museketeri wa Mutshamaxitulu wa Bodo ya Vahlayisi eka Independent Development Trust: Adv Kwazikwenkosi Mshengu (Mutshamaxitulu) na Manana Karabo Siyila (Xandla xa Mutshamaxitulu).

src: This year’s commemoration of Human Rights Month and Human Rights Day on 21 March takes place on the eve of the nation’s celebration of 30 Years of Freedom in April.
tgt: Leswi swa ha Taka N’hweti ya Timfanelo ta Vanhu Lembe leri ku tlangela N’hweti ya Timfanelo ta Vanhu na Siku ra Timfanelo ta Vanhu hi 21 Nyenyankulu swi ta va kona ku sale siku rin’we tiko ri nga si tlangela 30 wa Malembe ya Ntshuxeko hi Dzivamisoko.

src: Under the theme: “Three Decades of Respect for and Promotion of Human Rights”, Cabinet calls on everyone to play their part towards strengthening our human rights, and to cherish our freedom and democracy, which was attained at great cost.
tgt: Ehansi ka nhlokomhaka leyi nge: “Malembexikhume Manharhu ya ku Xixima na ku Hlohlotela Timfanelo ta Vanhu”, Khabinete yi rhamba hinkwavo ku teka xiave eka ku tiyisisa timfanelo ta hna ta ximunhu, na ku hoyozela ntshuxeko wa hina na demokirasi, leswi nga kumeka hi nxavo lowukulu.

src: District Development Model (DDM) Presidential Imbizo
tgt: Imbizo ya Puresidente ya Modelo wa Nhluvukiso wa Swifundzha (DDM) Puresidente u ta rhurhela Imbizo ya Puresidente ya DDM ya vu12 hi Ravumune, 7 Nyenyankulu 2024 eka Masipala wa Xifundzha xa Nkangala eMpumalanga.

src: c. The Imbizo brings together leaders from all three spheres of government to interact with residents on service delivery challenges and sets out plans for service delivery improvements and community development in the area.
tgt: Imbizo leyi yi hlanganisa varhangeri hinkwavo va swiyenge swinharhu swa mfumo ku ta tihlanganisa na vaaki eka swiphiqo swa mphakelo wa vukorhokeri na ku ta endla makungu yak u antswisa ku antswisa mphakelo wa vukorhokeri na nhluvukiso wa miganga endzhawini.

src: The DDM Presidential Imbizo and oversight visits have occurred in all nine provinces as part of efforts to reinforce on-going work of improving the lives of citizens.
tgt: Imbizo ya Puresidente ya DDM na maendzo ro landzellerisa swi vile kona eka swifundzhankulu hinkwaswo swa kaye tanihi matshalatshala yo tiyisisa ntirho lowu yaka emahlweni wa ku antswisa vutomi bya vaaki.

src: d. Cabinet calls on residents of the Nkangala District Municipality and surrounding areas to attend the Imbizo and engage their public representatives on issues affecting them.
tgt: Khabinete yi rhamba vatshami hinkwavo va le ka Masipala ya Xifundzha xa Nkangala na tindhawu ta le kusuhi ku va kona eka Imbizo na ku burisana na varhangeri va vona va mfumo mayelana na swiphiqo leswi va khumbaka.

src: Sustainable Infrastructure Development Symposium South Africa (SIDSSA) 2024 a.
tgt: Simphoziyamu ya Nhluvukiso wa Ntiyisiso wa Switirhisiwa eAfrika-Dzonga (SIDSSA) 2024 Sweswi swi le ka vufambisi hinkwabyo eka SIDSSA 2024,ley inga ta va kona eCape Town ku suka 17 ku fika 19 Nyenyankulu 2024.

src: The SIDSSA brings together critical role-players in the infrastructure sector who are key to accelerating the pace of infrastructure investments in the country.
tgt: SIDSSA yi hlanganisa vatekaxiave lavakulu eka xiyenge xa switirhisiwa lava va nga vona va nkoka eka ku hatlisisa magaoza ya vuvekisi bya switirhisiwa etikweni.

src: b. Infrastructure development has been the key priority of government and the Sixth Administration, as it contributes to economic growth and job creation.
tgt: Nhluvukiso wa switirhisiwa wu vile wa nkoka eka mfummo na le ka Vufambisi bya VUtsevu, tanihi loko swi hoxa xandla eka ku kula ka ku tumbuluxiwa ka mitirho.

src: The SIDSSA will showcase some of the progress in the implementation of the Infrastructure Investment Plan that was approved by Cabinet in May 2020.
tgt: SIDSSA yi ta kombisa yin’wana ya mihluvuko eku simekiweni ka Kungu ra Vuvekisi eka Switirhisiwa leri nga pfumelela hi Khabinete hi Mudyaxihi 2020.

src: Second Black Industrialists and Exporters Conference
tgt: Khoniferense ya Vumbirhi ya Van’watifeme na Vaxaviselamatiko ya Vantima Khoniferense ya Vumbirhi ya Van’watifeme na Vaxaviselamatiko ya Vantima yi ta va kona Sandton Convention Centre eJoni hi Ravunharhu, 20 Nyenyankulu 2024.

src: Messages Congratulations Cabinet extended its congratulations and well-wishes to: Ms Michelle Phillips on her appointment as the Group CEO of Transnet and Ms Nosipho Maphumulo as Group Chief Financial Officer of Transnet.
tgt: Khabinete yi khensa na ku navelela swa kahle eka: Manana Michelle Phillips eka ku thoriwa ka yena tanihi Ntlawa wa CEO eka Transnet na Manana Nosipho Maphumulo tanihi Ntlawa wa Mutamerinkulu wa Nkwama eTransnet.

src: These appointments are critical to the on-going work to rebuild the capacity within Transnet as part of the work to restore the country’s freight, rail and logistics capacity.
tgt: Ku thoriwa loku ku na nkoka eka ntirho wo yisa emahlweni ku aka nakambe vuswikoti eka Transnet tanihi xiphemu xa ntirho wo vuyisela vuswikoti bya tiko eka mindzhwalo, swifambo na vutleketli.

src: Mr. Wamkele Mene for his re-election as the Secretary General of the African Continental Free Trade Area Mr Sibusiso Ngalwa who is the current Chairperson of the South African National Editors Forum (SANEF) on his appointment to the Executive Committee of the Africa Editors Forum.
tgt: Tatana Wamkele Mene, eka ku hlawuriwa nakambe ku va Matsalaninkulu wa African Continental Free Trade Area.

src: Banyana-Banyana, the national women’s soccer team, for its victory in the second leg of the CAF Women’s Olympic Qualifiers.
tgt: Tatana Sibusiso Ngalwa, Mutshamaxitulu wa sweswi wa Foramu ya Rixaka ya Vahleri va Afrika-Dzonga (SANEF), eka ku thoriwa ka yena eka Komiti ya le Henhla ya African Editors’ Forum.

src: The team won the two-legged outing on a 4-0 on aggregate, and they will face Nigeria in the final round in April 2024.
tgt: Banyana Banyana, bolo ya milenge ya vavasati, eka ku hlula ka vona eka nenge wa vumbirhi wa CAF Women’s Olympic Qualifiers.

src: Condolences
tgt: Ku chavelela

src: Cabinet expressed condolences to the family, friends and colleagues of: Captain Simon Mkhulu Bobe and Lance Corporal Irven Thabang Semono of the South African National Defence Force, who were killed in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) on 14 February 2024.
tgt: Khabinete yi hundzisa ku chavelela ka yona eka maxaka, vanghana na vatirhikulobye va: Kaputeni Simon Mkhulu Bobe na Lance Corporal Irven Thabang Semon va Ndzawulo ya Vusirheleri ya Afrika-Dzonga, lava va nga dlayiwa eDemocratic Republic of Congo (DRC) hi 14 Nyenyanyana 2024.

src: They were part of the Southern African Development Community Mission in the DRC, commonly known as SAMIDRC deployed to restore security, peace, and stability in line with the AU Agenda of “Silencing the Guns by 2030”.
tgt: A va ri xiphemu xa Southern African Development Community Mission eDRC, leswi tiviwaka tanihi SAMIDRC, lava yisiweke ku ya vuyisela vuhlayiseki, ku rhula na ntshamiseko ku ya hi AU Agenda ya “Silencing the Guns by 2030”.

src: Cabinet also wished the three other soldiers injured in the attack a speedy recovery.
tgt: Nakambe Khabinete yi navelelea masocha laman’wana manharhu lava nga vaviseka leswaku va hatlisa va hola.

src: The Nine people from Mpumalanga who lost their lives in a tragic bus accident in Paul Pietersburg, KwaZulu-Natal from the African National Congress rally in eThekwini.
tgt: Kaye wa vanhu va le Mpumalanga lava nga lahlekela hi vutomi bya vona eka khombo ra movha ePaulpietersburg, KwaZulu-Natal loko va vuya eka rhali ya African National Congress eThekwini.

src: Issues from the Environment Economy Revenue collection Cabinet commends the millions of taxpayers who have filed their tax returns to help the South African Revenue Service collect tax revenue of R.155 trillion for the 2023/24 financial year.
tgt: Khabinete yi bumabumela mamiliyoni ya vahakelaxibalo lava nga fayila tifomoxibalo ku pfuna Vukorhokeri bya Xibalo bya Afrika-Dzonga ku hlengeleta mali ya xibalo ya R.155 wa tibiliyoni eka lembeximali ra 2023/.

src: This is R52 billion more than the previous year and demonstrates the robustness of the local economy, despite challenging local and international conditions.
tgt: Leswi swi tlula R52 wa tibiliyoni ku tlula lembe leri nga hundza naswona swi kombisa ku tiya ka ikhonomi ya laha kaya, hambileswi swiyimo swa laha kaya na swa matiko ya misava swi nga na ntlhontlho.

src: The increased revenue helps government to fund the country’s service-delivery projects and other socio-economic development programmes.
tgt: Mali leyi engetelekeke yi pfuna mfumo ku seketela hi timali tiphurojeke ta mphakelo wa vukorhokeri bya tiko na minongonoko yin’wana ya nhluvukiso wa ikhonomi ya vaaki.

src: Infrastructure investment Cabinet welcomed the opening of a R3,4 billion Newlyn Park Bayhead Rail Terminal project at the Port of Durban, which consists of 640 000 square metres of warehousing, rail sidings and open storage.
tgt: Khabinete yi amukerile ku pfuriwa ka phurojeke ya R3,4 wa tibiliyoni ta Xiporo xa Newlyn Park Bayhead Rail Terminal eRibuweni ra Durban, leyi nga na 640 000 wa swikweremitara swa vuhlayiselo, matlhelo ya swiporo na vuhlayiselo lebyi pfulekeke.

src: The new terminal will facilitate the efficient movement of sea, rail and road cargo through the Port of Durban, and help address the recent challenges experienced in the logistics, infrastructure and network industries.
tgt: Theminali leyintshwa yi ta fambisa ku fambafamba lokunene ka ndzhwalo wa le lwandle, swiporo na le magondzweni hi ku tirhisa Ribuwa ra Durban, na ku pfuneta ku lulamisa mitlhontlho ya sweswinyana leyi nga hlangana na yona eka tiindasitiri ta vutleketli, switirhisiwa na netiweke.

src: The investment resulted in 4 013 direct construction jobs and the full-time employment of more than 1 000 people, with this number expected to grow as the facility handles more cargo.
tgt: Vuvekisi byi endle leswaku ku va na 4 013 wa mitirho yo aka hi ku kongoma na ku thoriwa ka nkarhi hinkwawo ka vanhu vo tlula 1 000, laha nhlayo leyi yi languteriweke ku kula tanihileswi ndhawu leyi yi khomaka ndzhwalo wo tala.

src: In revitalising our country’s rail network, Cabinet also welcomed the Passenger Rail Agency of South Africa’s (PRASA) successful restoration of five crucial Metrorail services across Gauteng, KwaZulu-Natal and the Western Cape.
tgt: Eku pfuxeteni ka netiweke ya swiporo swa tiko ra hina, Khabinete yi tlhele yi amukela ku vuyiseriwa loku humelelaka ka Ejensi ya Switimela swo Rhwala Vanhu ya Afrika-Dzonga (PRASA) ya vukorhokeri bya ntlhanu bya nkoka bya Metrorail ku tsemakanya Gauteng, KwaZulu-Natal na Kapa-Vupeladyambu.

src: PRASA effectively brought 31 of its 40 lines back into partial operation and is working on achieving full operational status.
tgt: PRASA hi ndlela leyinene yi vuyisele 31 wa milayeni ya yona ya 40 eka ntirho wo karhi naswona yi le ku tirheni ku fikelela xiyimo xa ntirho hi ku hetiseka.

src: The milestone demonstrates government’s commitment to revitalising passenger rail services and providing an efficient public transport option for South Africans.
tgt: Nkoka lowu wu kombisa ku tinyiketela ka mfumo ku pfuxeta vukorhokeri bya switimela swo rhwala vanhu na ku nyika ndlela ya vutleketli bya mani na mani leyi tirhaka kahle eka MaAfrika-Dzonga.

src: In a related development, Cabinet welcomed the announcement by the South African National Roads Agency that it would inject over R50 billion into road infrastructure development in the Eastern Cape.
tgt: Eka nhluvukiso lowu yelanaka, Khabinete yi amukerile xitiviso hi Ejensi ya Magondzo ya Rixaka ya Afrika-Dzonga leswaku yi ta nghenisa ku tlula R50 wa tibiliyoni eka nhluvukiso wa switirhisiwa swa magondzo eKapa-Vuxa.

src: This infrastructure investment is geared towards the construction of new facilities, road improvements and strengthening, and special maintenance of the national road network in the province.
tgt: Vuvekisi lebyi bya switirhisiwa byi kongomisiwile eka ku akiwa ka switirhisiwa leswintshwa, ku antswisiwa ka magondzo na ku tiyisisiwa, na ku hlayisiwa ko hlawuleka ka netiweke ya magondzo ya rixaka eka xifundzankulu.

src: Investment Cabinet welcomed the opening of the new Tetra Pak facility in KwaZulu-Natal by President Cyril Ramaphosa, which attracted an investment of R500 million.
tgt: Vuvekisi Khabinete yi amukerile ku pfuriwa ka ndhawu leyintshwa ya Tetra Pak eKwaZulu-Natal hi Phuresidente Cyril Ramaphosa, leyi kokeke vuvekisi bya R500 wa timiliyoni.

src: The investment forms part of the Presidential Investment Mobilisation Drive where government set the ambitious target in 2018 to attract R1,2 trillion investments over five years.
tgt: Vuvekisi byi vumba xiphemu xa Pfhumba ro Hlengeleta Vuvekisi bya Phuresidente laha mfumo wu vekeke xikongomelo xa navelo hi 2018 ku koka rinoko ra vuvekisi bya R1,2 wa tibiliyoni ku tlula malembe ya ntlhanu.

src: Last year at the fifth South Africa Investment Conference, which marked end of the first phases of our investment mobilisation cycle, more the R1,5 trillion in investment commitments were raised.
tgt: Lembe leri nga hundza eka Khonferense ya Vuvekisi ya Afrika-Dzonga ya vuntlhanu, leyi nga fungha ku hela ka swiyenge swo sungula swa endlelo ra hina ro hlengeleta vuvekisi, ku hlengeletiwile ku tlula R1,5 wa tibiliyoni eka ku tinyiketela ka vuvekisi.

src: These investments translate into new factories, jobs in communities and greater economic activity around our country.
tgt: Vuvekisi lebyi byi hundzuluxela eka tifekitri letintshwa, mitirho emigangeni na migingiriko leyikulu ya ikhonomi ku rhendzela tiko ra hina.

src: Cabinet is confident that our investment drive will reignite economic growth and uplift our economy.
tgt: Khabinete yi na ku tshemba leswaku pfhumba ra hina ra vuvekisi ri ta pfuxeta ku kula ka ikhonomi na ku tlakusa ikhonomi ya hina.

src: Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF) Labour Activation Programme (LAP) Cabinet welcomed the launch of the UIF-LAP, which is a skills training and entrepreneurship programme aimed at benefitting the youth and the unemployed in the country.
tgt: Nongonoko Wo Tirhisa Vatirhi (LAP) Wa Nkwama Wa Ndzindzakhombo Wa Vaheleriwa Hi Ntirho (UIF)1.

src: The programme ensures that youth and work seekers are equipped with the necessary skills to be employable and to establish their own businesses.
tgt: Khabinete yi amukerile ku simekiwa ka UIF-LAP, leyi nga phurogireme ya ndzetelo wa vuswikoti na vubindzurisi leyi kongomisiweke eka ku vuyerisa vantshwa na lava pfumalaka mitirho etikweni.

src: The UIF-LAP, which will be rolled out across the country, is expected to create employment opportunities for over 704 000 unemployed people.
tgt: UIF-LAP, leyi nga ta hangalasiwa etikweni hinkwaro, yi languteriwile ku tumbuluxa mikateko ya mitirho eka ku tlula 704 000 wa vanhu lava nga tirhiki.

src: It will do so by providing training and small enterprise support to 333 projects across the country.
tgt: Yi ta endla tano hi ku nyika ndzetelo na nseketelo wa mabindzu lamatsongo eka tiphurojeke ta 333 etikweni hinkwaro.

src: About R.8 billion has been set aside to implement the plan and employment opportunities will run between 12 and 36 months.
tgt: Kwalomu ka R.8 wa tibiliyoni ti vekiwile etlhelo ku tirhisa pulani leyi naswona mikateko ya mitirho yi ta famba exikarhi ka 12 na 36 wa tin’hweti.

src: 30 Years of Freedom and Democracy Cabinet welcomed the launch of the commemoration of 30 Years of Freedom and Democracy, which is being held under the theme: “30 years of Democracy, Partnership and Growth”.
tgt: Malembe ya 30 ya Ntshunxeko na Xidemokirasi.

src: The launch also saw the unveiling of the official 30 Years of Freedom logo, which is a symbol that will unify us as we celebrate this significant milestone in the history of our country.
tgt: Khabinete yi amukerile ku simekiwa ka xitsundzuxo xa 30 wa Malembe ya Ntshunxeko na Xidemokirasi, lexi khomeriweke ehansi ka nhlokomhaka leyi nge: “30 wa malembe ya Xidemokirasi, Ntirhisano na ku Kula”.

src: Cabinet called on everyone to use the official logo which is available in various formats for ease of use on the GCIS website at: WEBTOKEN The launch marked the official commencement of the year-long activities to celebrate the remarkable progress we have made since 1994 in establishing a democratic society based on the Constitution of the Republic of South Africa of 1996 and the Bill of Rights.
tgt: Khabinete yi komberile un’wana na un’wana ku tirhisa logo ya ximfumo leyi kumekaka hi tifomati to hambana ku oloveriwa ku yi tirhisa eka webusayiti ya GCIS eka: WEBTOKEN.

src: This momentous occasion is also an opportunity to reflect on the challenges that remain and find ways to overcome them and move our country forward.
tgt: Ku simekiwa ku funghe ku sunguriwa ka ximfumo ka migingiriko ya lembe hinkwaro ku tlangela nhluvuko wo hlamarisa lowu hi wu endleke ku sukela hi 1994 eku simekeni ka rixaka ra xidemokirasi leri simekiweke eka Vumbiwa bya Riphabliki ra Afrika-Dzonga ra 1996 na Nawumbisi wa Timfanelo.

src: We have worked since 1994 to build a society based on unity and togetherness, and while many challenges still remain, conditions have fundamentally improved with each passing day.
tgt: Xiendlakalo lexi xa nkoka xi tlhela xi va nkarhi wo anakanyisisa hi mitlhontlho leyi nga sala na ku kuma tindlela to yi hlula na ku yisa tiko ra hina emahlweni.

src: The great strides we have made since 1994 are reflected in Census 2022 and the 30 Year Review.
tgt: Hi tirhile ku sukela hi 1994 ku aka rixaka leri simekiweke eka vun’we na ku va swin’we, naswona hambileswi mitlhontlho yo tala ya ha riki kona, swiyimo swi antswisiwile hi ku angarhela hi siku rin’wana na rin’wana leri hundzaka.

src: Both paint a picture of a society on the move and which reflects improvements across most indicators.
tgt: Nhluvuko lowukulu lowu hi wu endleke ku sukela hi 1994 wu kombisiwa eka Nhlayo ya Vanhu ya 2022 na Nkambisiso wa Malembe ya Havumbirhi bya tona ti kombisa rixaka leri yaka emahlweni naswona leri kombisaka ku antswisiwa eka swikombiso swo tala.

src: The findings of the Census and the 30 Year Review conclusively demonstrate that our development is not by chance, but rather by design from government programmes since 1994.
tgt: Swikumiwa swa Nhlayo ya Vanhu na Nkambisiso wa Malembe ya 30 swi kombisa hi ku hetiseka leswaku nhluvukiso wa hina a wu fikeleriwi hi xiwelo, kambe ematshan’weni ya sweswo wu fikeleriwa hi ku endliwa kusuka eka minongonoko ya mfumo ku sukela hi 1994.

src: Cabinet calls on all South Africans and sectors of society to participate in celebrating 30 Years of Freedom and Democracy.
tgt: Khabinete yi kombela MaAfrika-Dzonga hinkwavo na swiyenge swa vaaki ku nghenelela eku tlangeleni ka 30 wa Malembe ya Ntshunxeko na Xidemokirasi.

src: South Africans can participate by telling their stories on what it was like to have lived in apartheid South Africa and help us to build on the achievements we have made so far.
tgt: MaAfrika-Dzonga va nga nghenelela hi ku vula switori swa vona eka leswi a swi ri xiswona ku va hi hanye eAfrika-Dzonga ra xihlawuhlawu na ku hi pfuna ku aka eka ku humelela loku hi ku fikeleleke sweswi.

src: United Nations (UN) Human Rights Council Resolution Cabinet welcomes the UN Human Rights Council resolution calling for Israel to be held accountable for possible war crimes and crimes against humanity committed in Gaza.
tgt: Khabinete yi amukela xiboho xa Huvo ya Timfanelo ta Ximunhu xa Nhlangano wa Matiko lexi kombelaka leswaku Israel ri va na vutihlamuleri eka vugevenga bya nyimpi lebyi nga vaka kona na vugevenga byo lwisana na vumunhu lebyi endliweke eGaza.

src: The resolution further “called upon all States to cease the sale, transfer and diversion of arms, munitions and other military equipment to Israel”.
tgt: Xiboho lexi xi tlhele xi “kombela Matiko hinkwawo ku yimisa ku xavisiwa, ku hundzisela na ku hambukisiwa ka matlhari, swibamu na switirhisiwa swin’wana swa masocha eka Israel”.

src: The adoption of this resolution is historic as it is the very first time that the Human Rights Council has taken action on the unprecedented human tragedy taking place in Gaza, where at least 32 975 Palestinians have been killed, including more than 14 500 children, since Israel launched its onslaught over 180 days ago.
tgt: Ku amukeriwa ka xiboho lexi i ka matimu tanihileswi ku nga rosungula swinene leswaku Huvo ya Timfanelo ta Ximunhu yi teka magoza eka khombo ra ximunhu leri nga si tshamaka ri humelela eGaza, laha ku dlayiweke kwalomu ka 32 975 wa Mapalestina, ku katsa na vana vo tlula 14 500, ku sukela loko Israyele ri sungule nhlaselo wa rona eka masiku yo tlula 180 lama hundzeke.

src: 2024 General Elections It is all systems go for the 2024 National and Provincial Elections, following the signing of the Electoral Commission’s Code of Conduct by political parties and independent candidates.
tgt: I tisisiteme hinkwato ti yaka eka Nhlawulo wa Rixaka na wa Swifundzankulu wa 2024, endzhaku ka ku sayiniwa ka Nawu wa Matikhomelo wa Khomixini ya Nhlawulo hi mavandla ya tipolitiki na vahlawuriwa lava tiyimeleke.

src: The General Elections will be held on 29 May 2024 and in total 325 political parties will be taking part in this year’s elections.
tgt: Nhlawulo wa Mani na Mani wu ta khomiwa hi ti29 Mudyaxihi 2024 naswona hi ku angarhela 325 wa mavandla ya tipolitiki ya ta nghenelela eka nhlawulo wa lembe leri.

src: The Electoral Code of Conduct commits all those contesting the elections to abide by the set of rules that are meant to ensure free and fair elections.
tgt: Nawu wa Matikhomelo wa Nhlawulo wu boha hinkwavo lava phikizanaka eka nhlawulo ku landzelela xikatsa xa milawu leyi kongomisiweke ku tiyisisa nhlawulo lowu ntshunxekeke na ku lulama.

src: Cabinet is confident that our nation will once again build on our track record of holding regular, credible and free and fair national and local elections since 1994.
tgt: Khabinete yi na ku tshemba leswaku rixaka ra hina ri ta tlhela ri aka eka rhekhodo ya hina ya ku khoma nhlawulo wa rixaka na wa miganga wa nkarhi na nkarhi, lowu tshembekaka na lowu ntshunxekeke no lulama ku sukela hi 1994.

src: As the country celebrates 30 Years of Freedom, citizens are encouraged to exercise their democratic right and vote.
tgt: Tanihi leswi tiko ri tlangelaka 30 wa Malembe ya Ntshunxeko, vaaki va khutaziwa ku tirhisa mfanelo ya vona ya xidemokirasi na ku vhota.

src: National Artificial Intelligence (AI) Government Summit Rapid advances in AI are a reality and AI is rapidly shaping the world, which necessitates that countries prepare for its impact on citizens and governance systems.
tgt: Nhluvuko wa xihatla eka AI i ntiyiso naswona AI yi vumba misava hi xihatla, leswi lavaka leswaku matiko ya tilulamisela nkucetelo wa yona eka vaaki na tisisiteme ta vulawuri.

src: The National AI Government Summit was convened in Johannesburg on 5 April 2024 for government and the sector to initiate a policy and regulatory framework to guide and leverage advances in AI for human good.
tgt: Samiti ya Mfumo ya Rixaka ya AI yi vitaniwile eJoni hi ti5 Dzivamisoko 2024 leswaku mfumo na sekithara ku sungula pholisi na rimba ra milawu ku kongomisa na ku tirhisa nhluvuko eka AI ku pfuna vanhu.

src: AI policies are key to building a strong digital ecosystem in which governments, businesses and individuals can reap the benefits.
tgt: Tipholisi ta AI i xilotlelo xo aka ikhosisiteme ya xidijithali yo tiya laha mifumo, mabindzu na vanhu va nga tshovelaka mivuyelo.

src: The summit is the first step in charting a clear way forward towards leveraging the power of AI to address some of South Africa’s economic and social challenges.
tgt: Samiti i goza ro sungula ro hlela pulani ya maendlelo ya ndlela leyi nga erivaleni yo ya emahlweni eka ku tirhisa matimba ya AI ku lulamisa yin’wana ya mitlhontlho ya ikhonomi na ntshamiseko wa Afrika-Dzonga.

src: Crime and corruption Cabinet welcomed the signing into law of the Judicial Matters Amendment Act, 2023 (Act 15 of 2023).
tgt: Khabinete yi amukerile ku sayiniwa ka Ndzulamiso wa Nawu wa Timhaka ta Vuavanyisi, wa 2023 (Nawu wa 15 wa 2023) leswaku wu va nawu.

src: The Act gives effect to the recommendation of the State Capture Commission and creates an additional offence to be included in the Prevention and Combating of Corrupt Activities Act, 2004 (Act 12 of 2004) by holding individuals criminally liable for failure to prevent corruption.
tgt: Nawu wu nyika matimba eka xitsundzuxo xa Khomixini ya ku Vutliwa ka Matimba ya Mfumo na ku tumbuluxa nandzu wo engetela lowu nga ta katsiwa eka Nawu wa ku Sivela na ku Lwisana na Mitirho ya Vukungundzwana, wa 2004 (Nawu wa 12 wa 2004) hi ku khoma vanhu va ri na vutihlamuleri bya vugevenga byo tsandzeka ku sivela vukungundzwana.

src: The Act further aims to amend a number of Acts which are administered by the Department of Justice and Constitutional Development including powers, duties and functions of the Chief Master.
tgt: Nawu wu ya emahlweni wu kongomisa ku lulamisa Milawu yo hlaya leyi fambisiwaka hi Ndzawulo ya Vululami na Nhluvukiso wa Vumbiwa ku katsa na matimba, vutihlamuleri na mitirho ya Mufambisikulu.

src: These changes will allow the Chief Master to play a greater supervisory role over the Masters of the High Court and will lead to improved service delivery to the public and to legal practitioners.
tgt: Ku cinca loku ku ta pfumelela Mufambisikulu ku teka xiave lexikulu xa vulawuri eka Vafambisi va Khoto ya le Henhla naswona va ta rhangela ku yisa eka mphakelo wa vukorhokeri lowu antswisiweke eka vaaki na le ka vatirhi va swa nawu.

src: Updates to cabinet The status of the Road Accident Fund (RAF) Cabinet received a briefing on the implementation of the turnaround strategy for the RAF, aimed at simplifying the funds system while also improving the administration of benefits and payouts to accident victims.
