tgt: Khabinete yi amukerile ku nyikiwa ka vuxokoxoko mayelana na ku tirhisiwa ka maqhinga yo hundzula eka RAF, leyi kongomisiweke eka ku olovisa sisiteme ya timali loko yi ri karhi yi antswisa mafambiselo ya mivuyelo na ku hakeriwa ka vatwisiwakuvava hi tinghozi.

src: A key intervention has been the launch of the RAF contact centre, which provides a platform for RAF claimants to have access to their claims information without having to solely rely on their legal representatives.
tgt: Ku nghenelela ka nkoka ku vile ku simekiwa ka senthara ya vuhlanganisi ya RAF, leyi nyikaka pulatifomo eka vakomberi va RAF ku va na mfikelelo eka vuxokoxoko bya vona bya swikoxo handle ko titshega ntsena hi vayimeri va vona va nawu.

src: The platform also allows claimants the opportunity to verify the payments made by RAF to their legal representatives.
tgt: Pulatifomo ley yi tlhela yi pfumelela vakomberi ku kuma nkarhi wo tiyisisa tihakelo leti endliweke hi RAF eka vayimeri va vona va nawu.

src: The turnaround strategy has resulted in major improvements in the settlements of claims within 120 days, reduced legal costs by 75 percent and has seen a reduction of medical costs from R.6 billion in the 2019/20 financial year to R.1 billion in the 2023/24 financial year.
tgt: Qhinga ro cinca ri endle leswaku ku va na ku antswisiwa lokukulu eka ku hakeriwa ka swikoxo ku nga si hela masiku ya 120, ku hungutiwa ka tihakelo ta swa nawu hi 75 wa tiphesente naswona ri vonile ku hunguteka ka tihakelo ta vutshunguri kusuka eka R.6 wa tibiliyoni eka lembe ximali ra 2019/20 ku ya eka R.1 wa tibiliyoni eka lembe ximali ra 2023/24.

src: The interventions also led to a cumulative legal costs savings of over R23 billion in the three years of implementing the strategy.
tgt: Ku nghenelela ku tlhele ku yisa eka ku hlayisiwa ka mali leyi hlengeletiweke ya tihakelo ta swa nawu ku tlula R23 wa tibiliyoni eka malembe manharhu ya ku tirhisa maqhinga.

src: Moreover, the strategy interventions resulted in the in the reduction of claims paid to claimants/ short term liability to R.3 billion for the period ending 31 March 2023.
tgt: Ku tlula kwalaho, ku nghenelela ka maqhinga ku endle leswaku ku hungutiwa swikoxo leswi hakeriwaka eka vakomberi/ vutihlamuleri bya nkarhi wo koma ku ya eka R.3 wa tibiliyoni eka nkarhi lowu helaka hi ti31 Nyenyankulu 2023.

src: Cabinet was also updated on legislative amendments to the current RAF Act, which are at an advanced stage.
tgt: Khabinete yi tlhele yi pfuxetiwa hi ku lulamisiwa ka milawu eka Nawu wa sweswi wa RAF, lowu nga eka xiyimo xa le henhla.

src: The RAF Amendment Bill will be considered by the 7th administration of government.
tgt: Ndzulamiso wa Nawumbisi wa RAF wu ta langutiwa hi vufambisi bya vu7 bya mfumo.

src: The bill is aimed at refining the benefits and the payment of certain products in annuities and making it equitable.
tgt: Nawumbisi lowu wu kongomisiwile eka ku antswisa mivuyelo na ku hakeriwa ka swikumiwa swo karhi eka swipfuno swa mali na ku endla leswaku swi ringana.

src: Cabinet decisions White Paper on Citizenship, Immigration and Refugee Protection Cabinet approved the White Paper on Citizenship, Immigration and Refugee Protection for implementation, following a wide consultation process undertaken by the Department of Home Affairs in all nine provinces.
tgt: Khabinete yi pasisile Nawumbisi wa Vuakatiko, Vuhlapfa na Nsirhelelo wa Vahlapfa ku tirhisiwa, endzhaku ka endlelo ro anama ra ku burisana leri endliweke hi Ndzawulo ya Timhaka ta Xikaya eka swifundzankulu hinkwaswo swa kaye.

src: The policy aims to provide a framework to guide citizenship, immigration and refugee protection, considering the country’s national security interests and in compliance with international agreements and protocols on migration that South Africa is party to.
tgt: Pholisi yi kongomisa ku nyika rimba ro letela vuakatiko, vuhlapfa na nsirhelelo wa vahlapfa, ku tekela enhlokweni ku tsakela ka vusirheleri bya rixaka bya tiko na ku landzelerisa mitwanano ya matiko ya misava na tiphrothokholi ta vuhlapfa leti Afrika-Dzonga ri nga xiphemu eka tona.

src: It will also promote South Africa’s economic interests, transformation and job creation efforts.
tgt: Swi ta tlhela swi tlakusa ku tsakela ka ikhonomi ya Afrika-Dzonga, ku cinca na matshalatshala yo tumbuluxa mitirho.

src: Towards a 30-Year Review of South Africa’s Democracy (1994-2024).
tgt: Ku Kongoma eka Nkambisiso wa Malembe ya 30 wa Xidemokirasi xa Afrika-Dzonga (1994-2024).

src: Cabinet approved the publication of the report “Towards a 30-Year Review of South Africa’s Democracy (1994-2024)”.
tgt: Khabinete yi pasisile ku kandziyisiwa ka xiviko lexi nge “Ku Kongoma eka Nkambisiso wa Malembe ya 30 wa Xidemokirasi xa Afrika-Dzonga (1994-2024)”.

src: The review report heralds the story of South Africa’s transition into democracy since the historical elections of 27 April 1994.
tgt: Xiviko xa nkambisiso xi tivisa xitori xa ku cinca ka Afrika-Dzonga eka xidemokirasi ku sukela eka nhlawulo wa matimu wa ti27 Dzivamisoko 1994.

src: South Africa’s story of transition to democracy continues to inspire hope for many people around the world, and the review report highlights important lessons in the evolution of our democracy.
tgt: Xitori xa Afrika-Dzonga xa ku cinca eka xidemokirasi xi ya emahlweni xi hlohlotela ntshembo eka vanhu vo tala emisaveni hinkwayo, naswona xiviko xa nkambisiso xi kombisa tidyondzo ta nkoka eka ku hundzuka ka xidemokirasi xa hina.

src: Over the last 30 years, the country has attained a stable democracy, with strong institutions and a considerable global influence.
tgt: Eka malembe ya 30 lama hundzeke, tiko ri fikelerile xidemokirasi lexi tiyeke, lexi nga na mavandla yo tiya na nkucetelo lowukulu wa misava hinkwayo.

src: The 30-Year Review Report is structured on 13 thematic areas informed by four important references (1) the 1994 Reconstruction and Development Programme and its five objectives (2) the 1996 adoption of the Constitution (3) the 2012 National Development Plan and (4) the Medium-Term Strategic Framework 2019-2024 to reflect seven priorities of the sixth administration.
tgt: Xiviko xa Nkambisiso wa Malembe ya 30 xi hlengeletiwile eka tindhawu ta 13 ta nhlokomhaka leti tivisiweke hi swikombiso swa mune swa nkoka (1) Nongonoko wa ku aka hi Vuntshwa na Nhluvukiso wa 1994 na swikongomelo swa wona swa ntlhanu (2) ku amukeriwa ka Vumbiwa hi 1996 (3) Kungu ra Nhluvukiso wa Rixaka ra 2012 na (4) Rimba ra Maqhinga ra Nkarhi wa le Xikarhi ra 2019-2024 ku kombisa swilo swa nkoka swa nkombo swa vufambisi bya vutsevu.

src: The review report will be published by the Department of Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation and members of society will have an opportunity to engage the report.
tgt: Xiviko xa nkambisiso xi ta kandziyisiwa hi Ndzawulo ya Vupulani, Vulawuri na Nkambisiso naswona swirho swa vaaki swi ta va na nkarhi wo nghenelela eka xiviko.

src: Upcoming Events 6th Commonwealth Red Cross and Red Crescent Conference on International Humanitarian Law South Africa and the International Committee of the Red Cross will co-host the 6th Red Cross and Red Crescent Commonwealth Conference on International Humanitarian Law in South Africa from 15 to 19 April 2024 at the Irene Country Lodge in Pretoria.
tgt: Migingiriko leyi nga ta Landzela Khonferense ya vu6 ya Xihambano xo Tshwuka na N’weti wo Tshwuka ya Nhlangano wa Matiko eka Nawu wa Matiko ya Misava wa Vumunhu.1 Afrika-Dzonga na Komiti ya Matiko ya Misava ya Xihambano xo Tshwuka va ta rhurhela swin’we Khonferense ya vu6 ya Xihambano xo Tshwuka na N’weti wo Tshwuka wa Nhlangano wa Nawu wa Matiko ya Misava eAfrika-Dzonga ku sukela hi ti15 ku fikela hi ti19 Dzivamisoko 2024 eIrene Country Lodge ePitori.

src: The conference will bring together representatives of Commonwealth Member States, members of the Red Cross and Red Crescent movement, and other key stakeholders to deliberate on International Human Law.
tgt: Khonferense yi ta hlanganisa vayimeri va Matiko ya Swirho swa Nhlangano wa Matiko, swirho swa nhlangano wa Xihambano xo Tshwuka na N’weti wo Tshwuka, na vatekaxiave van’wana va nkoka ku burisana hi Nawu wa Vanhu wa Matiko ya Misava.

src: The conference seeks to recalibrate and strengthen existing human rights instruments and deepen our knowledge on the importance of International Human Law in an era of increased armed conflicts as well as climate change, food insecurity and growing displacement.
tgt: Khonferense yi lava ku cinca nakambe ndlela ya maendlelo na ku tiyisisa switirhisiwa swa timfanelo ta ximunhu leswi nga kona na ku dzikisa vutivi bya hina eka nkoka wa Nawu wa Vanhu wa Matiko ya Misava eka nguva ya ku engeteleka ka tinyimpi leti hlomeke xikan’we na ku cinca ka maxelo, ku pfumaleka ka swakudya na ku rhurha loku kulaka.

src: Cabinet extended its congratulations and well-wishes to: Health Minister Dr Joe Phaahla on his appointment to the Global Fund Board effective from 1 May 2024.
tgt: Mahungu Ku hoyozelaKhabinete yi hundzisa mahungu ya yona yo hoyozela ni ku navelela mikateko eka:• Holobye wa Rihanyo Dkd Joe Phaahla eka ku thoriwa ka yena eka Huvo ya Nkwama wa Misava hinkwayo ku sukela hi ti1 Mudyaxihi 2024.

src: Dr Phaahla will serve as a representative of the East and Southern Africa region.
tgt: Dkd Phaahla u ta tirha tanihi muyimeri wa xifundzankulu xa Afrika-Vuxa na Dzonga.• Mamozileme ya MaAfrika-Dzonga xikan’we na lava va nga emisaveni hinkwayo, ngopfungopfu ePalestina, hi xiendlakalo xa Eid al-Fitr.

src: South Africans Muslims as well as those across the globe, especially in Palestine, on the occasion of Eid al-Fitr.
tgt: Ramadan nakambe i nkarhi wa ku anakanyisisa endzeni, ku pfuna na ku tinyiketela ka ximoya loko Mamozileme ya lwela ku kula ka ximoya na ku tikhoma.

src: Ramadan is also a time of inner reflection, charity and spiritual devotion when Muslims strive towards spiritual growth and self-control.
tgt: Nkhuvo wa Eid al-Fitr wu fungha makumu ya n’hweti yo kwetsima ya Ramadan, leyi hi nkarhi wa yona Mamozileme ma titsone swakudya siku na siku, naswona ehansi ka swiyimo swo tika swinene ePalestina.• Khomixini ya Mphikizano ya Afrika-Dzonga hi ku wina masagwadi mambirhi eka Masagwadi ya ku Tsala ya Antitrust ya 2024 leyi khomeriweke eWashington DC na ku xiximiwa eka Vulavisisi bya yona bya Makete bya Tipulatifomo ta Vuhlanganisi bya le ka Inthanete lebyi rhangelaka.

src: The festival of Eid al-Fitr marks the culmination of the holy month of Ramadan, during which Muslims have fasted daily, and under extreme conditions in Palestine.
tgt: Yi hlurile sagwadi eka xiviko xa yona xo hetelela na xiboho kasi sagwadi rin’wana a ri ri ra atikili ya dyondzo eka ku cinca-cinca ka mphikizano eka timakete ta xidijithali ta Afrika-Dzonga eka tendzo na vupfhumba.

src: Issues from the Environment Economy Revenue collection Cabinet commends the millions of taxpayers who have filed their tax returns to help the South African Revenue Service collect tax revenue of R.155 trillion for the 2023/24 financial year.
tgt: Khabinete yi bumabumela mamiliyoni ya vahakelaxibalo lava nga fayila tifomoxibalo ku pfuna Vukorhokeri bya Xibalo bya Afrika-Dzonga ku hlengeleta mali ya xibalo ya R.155 wa tibiliyoni eka lembeximali ra 2023/.

src: This is R52 billion more than the previous year and demonstrates the robustness of the local economy, despite challenging local and international conditions.
tgt: Leswi swi tlula R52 wa tibiliyoni ku tlula lembe leri nga hundza naswona swi kombisa ku tiya ka ikhonomi ya laha kaya, hambileswi swiyimo swa laha kaya na swa matiko ya misava swi nga na ntlhontlho.

src: The increased revenue helps government to fund the country’s service-delivery projects and other socio-economic development programmes.
tgt: Mali leyi engetelekeke yi pfuna mfumo ku seketela hi timali tiphurojeke ta mphakelo wa vukorhokeri bya tiko na minongonoko yin’wana ya nhluvukiso wa ikhonomi ya vaaki.

src: Infrastructure investment Cabinet welcomed the opening of a R3,4 billion Newlyn Park Bayhead Rail Terminal project at the Port of Durban, which consists of 640 000 square metres of warehousing, rail sidings and open storage.
tgt: Khabinete yi amukerile ku pfuriwa ka phurojeke ya R3,4 wa tibiliyoni ta Xiporo xa Newlyn Park Bayhead Rail Terminal eRibuweni ra Durban, leyi nga na 640 000 wa swikweremitara swa vuhlayiselo, matlhelo ya swiporo na vuhlayiselo lebyi pfulekeke.

src: The new terminal will facilitate the efficient movement of sea, rail and road cargo through the Port of Durban, and help address the recent challenges experienced in the logistics, infrastructure and network industries.
tgt: Theminali leyintshwa yi ta fambisa ku fambafamba lokunene ka ndzhwalo wa le lwandle, swiporo na le magondzweni hi ku tirhisa Ribuwa ra Durban, na ku pfuneta ku lulamisa mitlhontlho ya sweswinyana leyi nga hlangana na yona eka tiindasitiri ta vutleketli, switirhisiwa na netiweke.

src: The investment resulted in 4 013 direct construction jobs and the full-time employment of more than 1 000 people, with this number expected to grow as the facility handles more cargo.
tgt: Vuvekisi byi endle leswaku ku va na 4 013 wa mitirho yo aka hi ku kongoma na ku thoriwa ka nkarhi hinkwawo ka vanhu vo tlula 1 000, laha nhlayo leyi yi languteriweke ku kula tanihileswi ndhawu leyi yi khomaka ndzhwalo wo tala.

src: In revitalising our country’s rail network, Cabinet also welcomed the Passenger Rail Agency of South Africa’s (PRASA) successful restoration of five crucial Metrorail services across Gauteng, KwaZulu-Natal and the Western Cape.
tgt: Eku pfuxeteni ka netiweke ya swiporo swa tiko ra hina, Khabinete yi tlhele yi amukela ku vuyiseriwa loku humelelaka ka Ejensi ya Switimela swo Rhwala Vanhu ya Afrika-Dzonga (PRASA) ya vukorhokeri bya ntlhanu bya nkoka bya Metrorail ku tsemakanya Gauteng, KwaZulu-Natal na Kapa-Vupeladyambu.

src: PRASA effectively brought 31 of its 40 lines back into partial operation and is working on achieving full operational status.
tgt: PRASA hi ndlela leyinene yi vuyisele 31 wa milayeni ya yona ya 40 eka ntirho wo karhi naswona yi le ku tirheni ku fikelela xiyimo xa ntirho hi ku hetiseka.

src: The milestone demonstrates government’s commitment to revitalising passenger rail services and providing an efficient public transport option for South Africans.
tgt: Nkoka lowu wu kombisa ku tinyiketela ka mfumo ku pfuxeta vukorhokeri bya switimela swo rhwala vanhu na ku nyika ndlela ya vutleketli bya mani na mani leyi tirhaka kahle eka MaAfrika-Dzonga.

src: In a related development, Cabinet welcomed the announcement by the South African National Roads Agency that it would inject over R50 billion into road infrastructure development in the Eastern Cape.
tgt: Eka nhluvukiso lowu yelanaka, Khabinete yi amukerile xitiviso hi Ejensi ya Magondzo ya Rixaka ya Afrika-Dzonga leswaku yi ta nghenisa ku tlula R50 wa tibiliyoni eka nhluvukiso wa switirhisiwa swa magondzo eKapa-Vuxa.

src: This infrastructure investment is geared towards the construction of new facilities, road improvements and strengthening, and special maintenance of the national road network in the province.
tgt: Vuvekisi lebyi bya switirhisiwa byi kongomisiwile eka ku akiwa ka switirhisiwa leswintshwa, ku antswisiwa ka magondzo na ku tiyisisiwa, na ku hlayisiwa ko hlawuleka ka netiweke ya magondzo ya rixaka eka xifundzankulu.

src: Investment Cabinet welcomed the opening of the new Tetra Pak facility in KwaZulu-Natal by President Cyril Ramaphosa, which attracted an investment of R500 million.
tgt: Vuvekisi Khabinete yi amukerile ku pfuriwa ka ndhawu leyintshwa ya Tetra Pak eKwaZulu-Natal hi Phuresidente Cyril Ramaphosa, leyi kokeke vuvekisi bya R500 wa timiliyoni.

src: The investment forms part of the Presidential Investment Mobilisation Drive where government set the ambitious target in 2018 to attract R1,2 trillion investments over five years.
tgt: Vuvekisi byi vumba xiphemu xa Pfhumba ro Hlengeleta Vuvekisi bya Phuresidente laha mfumo wu vekeke xikongomelo xa navelo hi 2018 ku koka rinoko ra vuvekisi bya R1,2 wa tibiliyoni ku tlula malembe ya ntlhanu.

src: Last year at the fifth South Africa Investment Conference, which marked end of the first phases of our investment mobilisation cycle, more the R1,5 trillion in investment commitments were raised.
tgt: Lembe leri nga hundza eka Khonferense ya Vuvekisi ya Afrika-Dzonga ya vuntlhanu, leyi nga fungha ku hela ka swiyenge swo sungula swa endlelo ra hina ro hlengeleta vuvekisi, ku hlengeletiwile ku tlula R1,5 wa tibiliyoni eka ku tinyiketela ka vuvekisi.

src: These investments translate into new factories, jobs in communities and greater economic activity around our country.
tgt: Vuvekisi lebyi byi hundzuluxela eka tifekitri letintshwa, mitirho emigangeni na migingiriko leyikulu ya ikhonomi ku rhendzela tiko ra hina.

src: Cabinet is confident that our investment drive will reignite economic growth and uplift our economy.
tgt: Khabinete yi na ku tshemba leswaku pfhumba ra hina ra vuvekisi ri ta pfuxeta ku kula ka ikhonomi na ku tlakusa ikhonomi ya hina.

src: Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF) Labour Activation Programme (LAP) Cabinet welcomed the launch of the UIF-LAP, which is a skills training and entrepreneurship programme aimed at benefitting the youth and the unemployed in the country.
tgt: Nongonoko Wo Tirhisa Vatirhi (LAP) Wa Nkwama Wa Ndzindzakhombo Wa Vaheleriwa Hi Ntirho (UIF)1.

src: The programme ensures that youth and work seekers are equipped with the necessary skills to be employable and to establish their own businesses.
tgt: Khabinete yi amukerile ku simekiwa ka UIF-LAP, leyi nga phurogireme ya ndzetelo wa vuswikoti na vubindzurisi leyi kongomisiweke eka ku vuyerisa vantshwa na lava pfumalaka mitirho etikweni.

src: The UIF-LAP, which will be rolled out across the country, is expected to create employment opportunities for over 704 000 unemployed people.
tgt: UIF-LAP, leyi nga ta hangalasiwa etikweni hinkwaro, yi languteriwile ku tumbuluxa mikateko ya mitirho eka ku tlula 704 000 wa vanhu lava nga tirhiki.

src: It will do so by providing training and small enterprise support to 333 projects across the country.
tgt: Yi ta endla tano hi ku nyika ndzetelo na nseketelo wa mabindzu lamatsongo eka tiphurojeke ta 333 etikweni hinkwaro.

src: About R.8 billion has been set aside to implement the plan and employment opportunities will run between 12 and 36 months.
tgt: Kwalomu ka R.8 wa tibiliyoni ti vekiwile etlhelo ku tirhisa pulani leyi naswona mikateko ya mitirho yi ta famba exikarhi ka 12 na 36 wa tin’hweti.

src: 30 Years of Freedom and Democracy Cabinet welcomed the launch of the commemoration of 30 Years of Freedom and Democracy, which is being held under the theme: “30 years of Democracy, Partnership and Growth”.
tgt: Malembe ya 30 ya Ntshunxeko na Xidemokirasi.

src: The launch also saw the unveiling of the official 30 Years of Freedom logo, which is a symbol that will unify us as we celebrate this significant milestone in the history of our country.
tgt: Khabinete yi amukerile ku simekiwa ka xitsundzuxo xa 30 wa Malembe ya Ntshunxeko na Xidemokirasi, lexi khomeriweke ehansi ka nhlokomhaka leyi nge: “30 wa malembe ya Xidemokirasi, Ntirhisano na ku Kula”.

src: Cabinet called on everyone to use the official logo which is available in various formats for ease of use on the GCIS website at: WEBTOKEN The launch marked the official commencement of the year-long activities to celebrate the remarkable progress we have made since 1994 in establishing a democratic society based on the Constitution of the Republic of South Africa of 1996 and the Bill of Rights.
tgt: Khabinete yi komberile un’wana na un’wana ku tirhisa logo ya ximfumo leyi kumekaka hi tifomati to hambana ku oloveriwa ku yi tirhisa eka webusayiti ya GCIS eka: WEBTOKEN.

src: This momentous occasion is also an opportunity to reflect on the challenges that remain and find ways to overcome them and move our country forward.
tgt: Ku simekiwa ku funghe ku sunguriwa ka ximfumo ka migingiriko ya lembe hinkwaro ku tlangela nhluvuko wo hlamarisa lowu hi wu endleke ku sukela hi 1994 eku simekeni ka rixaka ra xidemokirasi leri simekiweke eka Vumbiwa bya Riphabliki ra Afrika-Dzonga ra 1996 na Nawumbisi wa Timfanelo.

src: We have worked since 1994 to build a society based on unity and togetherness, and while many challenges still remain, conditions have fundamentally improved with each passing day.
tgt: Xiendlakalo lexi xa nkoka xi tlhela xi va nkarhi wo anakanyisisa hi mitlhontlho leyi nga sala na ku kuma tindlela to yi hlula na ku yisa tiko ra hina emahlweni.

src: The great strides we have made since 1994 are reflected in Census 2022 and the 30 Year Review.
tgt: Hi tirhile ku sukela hi 1994 ku aka rixaka leri simekiweke eka vun’we na ku va swin’we, naswona hambileswi mitlhontlho yo tala ya ha riki kona, swiyimo swi antswisiwile hi ku angarhela hi siku rin’wana na rin’wana leri hundzaka.

src: Both paint a picture of a society on the move and which reflects improvements across most indicators.
tgt: Nhluvuko lowukulu lowu hi wu endleke ku sukela hi 1994 wu kombisiwa eka Nhlayo ya Vanhu ya 2022 na Nkambisiso wa Malembe ya Havumbirhi bya tona ti kombisa rixaka leri yaka emahlweni naswona leri kombisaka ku antswisiwa eka swikombiso swo tala.

src: The findings of the Census and the 30 Year Review conclusively demonstrate that our development is not by chance, but rather by design from government programmes since 1994.
tgt: Swikumiwa swa Nhlayo ya Vanhu na Nkambisiso wa Malembe ya 30 swi kombisa hi ku hetiseka leswaku nhluvukiso wa hina a wu fikeleriwi hi xiwelo, kambe ematshan’weni ya sweswo wu fikeleriwa hi ku endliwa kusuka eka minongonoko ya mfumo ku sukela hi 1994.

src: Cabinet calls on all South Africans and sectors of society to participate in celebrating 30 Years of Freedom and Democracy.
tgt: Khabinete yi kombela MaAfrika-Dzonga hinkwavo na swiyenge swa vaaki ku nghenelela eku tlangeleni ka 30 wa Malembe ya Ntshunxeko na Xidemokirasi.

src: South Africans can participate by telling their stories on what it was like to have lived in apartheid South Africa and help us to build on the achievements we have made so far.
tgt: MaAfrika-Dzonga va nga nghenelela hi ku vula switori swa vona eka leswi a swi ri xiswona ku va hi hanye eAfrika-Dzonga ra xihlawuhlawu na ku hi pfuna ku aka eka ku humelela loku hi ku fikeleleke sweswi.

src: United Nations (UN) Human Rights Council Resolution Cabinet welcomes the UN Human Rights Council resolution calling for Israel to be held accountable for possible war crimes and crimes against humanity committed in Gaza.
tgt: Khabinete yi amukela xiboho xa Huvo ya Timfanelo ta Ximunhu xa Nhlangano wa Matiko lexi kombelaka leswaku Israel ri va na vutihlamuleri eka vugevenga bya nyimpi lebyi nga vaka kona na vugevenga byo lwisana na vumunhu lebyi endliweke eGaza.

src: The resolution further “called upon all States to cease the sale, transfer and diversion of arms, munitions and other military equipment to Israel”.
tgt: Xiboho lexi xi tlhele xi “kombela Matiko hinkwawo ku yimisa ku xavisiwa, ku hundzisela na ku hambukisiwa ka matlhari, swibamu na switirhisiwa swin’wana swa masocha eka Israel”.

src: The adoption of this resolution is historic as it is the very first time that the Human Rights Council has taken action on the unprecedented human tragedy taking place in Gaza, where at least 32 975 Palestinians have been killed, including more than 14 500 children, since Israel launched its onslaught over 180 days ago.
tgt: Ku amukeriwa ka xiboho lexi i ka matimu tanihileswi ku nga rosungula swinene leswaku Huvo ya Timfanelo ta Ximunhu yi teka magoza eka khombo ra ximunhu leri nga si tshamaka ri humelela eGaza, laha ku dlayiweke kwalomu ka 32 975 wa Mapalestina, ku katsa na vana vo tlula 14 500, ku sukela loko Israyele ri sungule nhlaselo wa rona eka masiku yo tlula 180 lama hundzeke.

src: 2024 General Elections It is all systems go for the 2024 National and Provincial Elections, following the signing of the Electoral Commission’s Code of Conduct by political parties and independent candidates.
tgt: I tisisiteme hinkwato ti yaka eka Nhlawulo wa Rixaka na wa Swifundzankulu wa 2024, endzhaku ka ku sayiniwa ka Nawu wa Matikhomelo wa Khomixini ya Nhlawulo hi mavandla ya tipolitiki na vahlawuriwa lava tiyimeleke.

src: The General Elections will be held on 29 May 2024 and in total 325 political parties will be taking part in this year’s elections.
tgt: Nhlawulo wa Mani na Mani wu ta khomiwa hi ti29 Mudyaxihi 2024 naswona hi ku angarhela 325 wa mavandla ya tipolitiki ya ta nghenelela eka nhlawulo wa lembe leri.

src: The Electoral Code of Conduct commits all those contesting the elections to abide by the set of rules that are meant to ensure free and fair elections.
tgt: Nawu wa Matikhomelo wa Nhlawulo wu boha hinkwavo lava phikizanaka eka nhlawulo ku landzelela xikatsa xa milawu leyi kongomisiweke ku tiyisisa nhlawulo lowu ntshunxekeke na ku lulama.

src: Cabinet is confident that our nation will once again build on our track record of holding regular, credible and free and fair national and local elections since 1994.
tgt: Khabinete yi na ku tshemba leswaku rixaka ra hina ri ta tlhela ri aka eka rhekhodo ya hina ya ku khoma nhlawulo wa rixaka na wa miganga wa nkarhi na nkarhi, lowu tshembekaka na lowu ntshunxekeke no lulama ku sukela hi 1994.

src: As the country celebrates 30 Years of Freedom, citizens are encouraged to exercise their democratic right and vote.
tgt: Tanihi leswi tiko ri tlangelaka 30 wa Malembe ya Ntshunxeko, vaaki va khutaziwa ku tirhisa mfanelo ya vona ya xidemokirasi na ku vhota.

src: National Artificial Intelligence (AI) Government Summit Rapid advances in AI are a reality and AI is rapidly shaping the world, which necessitates that countries prepare for its impact on citizens and governance systems.
tgt: Nhluvuko wa xihatla eka AI i ntiyiso naswona AI yi vumba misava hi xihatla, leswi lavaka leswaku matiko ya tilulamisela nkucetelo wa yona eka vaaki na tisisiteme ta vulawuri.

src: The National AI Government Summit was convened in Johannesburg on 5 April 2024 for government and the sector to initiate a policy and regulatory framework to guide and leverage advances in AI for human good.
tgt: Samiti ya Mfumo ya Rixaka ya AI yi vitaniwile eJoni hi ti5 Dzivamisoko 2024 leswaku mfumo na sekithara ku sungula pholisi na rimba ra milawu ku kongomisa na ku tirhisa nhluvuko eka AI ku pfuna vanhu.

src: AI policies are key to building a strong digital ecosystem in which governments, businesses and individuals can reap the benefits.
tgt: Tipholisi ta AI i xilotlelo xo aka ikhosisiteme ya xidijithali yo tiya laha mifumo, mabindzu na vanhu va nga tshovelaka mivuyelo.

src: The summit is the first step in charting a clear way forward towards leveraging the power of AI to address some of South Africa’s economic and social challenges.
tgt: Samiti i goza ro sungula ro hlela pulani ya maendlelo ya ndlela leyi nga erivaleni yo ya emahlweni eka ku tirhisa matimba ya AI ku lulamisa yin’wana ya mitlhontlho ya ikhonomi na ntshamiseko wa Afrika-Dzonga.

src: Crime and corruption Cabinet welcomed the signing into law of the Judicial Matters Amendment Act, 2023 (Act 15 of 2023).
tgt: Khabinete yi amukerile ku sayiniwa ka Ndzulamiso wa Nawu wa Timhaka ta Vuavanyisi, wa 2023 (Nawu wa 15 wa 2023) leswaku wu va nawu.

src: The Act gives effect to the recommendation of the State Capture Commission and creates an additional offence to be included in the Prevention and Combating of Corrupt Activities Act, 2004 (Act 12 of 2004) by holding individuals criminally liable for failure to prevent corruption.
tgt: Nawu wu nyika matimba eka xitsundzuxo xa Khomixini ya ku Vutliwa ka Matimba ya Mfumo na ku tumbuluxa nandzu wo engetela lowu nga ta katsiwa eka Nawu wa ku Sivela na ku Lwisana na Mitirho ya Vukungundzwana, wa 2004 (Nawu wa 12 wa 2004) hi ku khoma vanhu va ri na vutihlamuleri bya vugevenga byo tsandzeka ku sivela vukungundzwana.

src: The Act further aims to amend a number of Acts which are administered by the Department of Justice and Constitutional Development including powers, duties and functions of the Chief Master.
tgt: Nawu wu ya emahlweni wu kongomisa ku lulamisa Milawu yo hlaya leyi fambisiwaka hi Ndzawulo ya Vululami na Nhluvukiso wa Vumbiwa ku katsa na matimba, vutihlamuleri na mitirho ya Mufambisikulu.

src: These changes will allow the Chief Master to play a greater supervisory role over the Masters of the High Court and will lead to improved service delivery to the public and to legal practitioners.
tgt: Ku cinca loku ku ta pfumelela Mufambisikulu ku teka xiave lexikulu xa vulawuri eka Vafambisi va Khoto ya le Henhla naswona va ta rhangela ku yisa eka mphakelo wa vukorhokeri lowu antswisiweke eka vaaki na le ka vatirhi va swa nawu.

src: Updates to cabinet The status of the Road Accident Fund (RAF) Cabinet received a briefing on the implementation of the turnaround strategy for the RAF, aimed at simplifying the funds system while also improving the administration of benefits and payouts to accident victims.
tgt: Khabinete yi amukerile ku nyikiwa ka vuxokoxoko mayelana na ku tirhisiwa ka maqhinga yo hundzula eka RAF, leyi kongomisiweke eka ku olovisa sisiteme ya timali loko yi ri karhi yi antswisa mafambiselo ya mivuyelo na ku hakeriwa ka vatwisiwakuvava hi tinghozi.

src: A key intervention has been the launch of the RAF contact centre, which provides a platform for RAF claimants to have access to their claims information without having to solely rely on their legal representatives.
tgt: Ku nghenelela ka nkoka ku vile ku simekiwa ka senthara ya vuhlanganisi ya RAF, leyi nyikaka pulatifomo eka vakomberi va RAF ku va na mfikelelo eka vuxokoxoko bya vona bya swikoxo handle ko titshega ntsena hi vayimeri va vona va nawu.

src: The platform also allows claimants the opportunity to verify the payments made by RAF to their legal representatives.
tgt: Pulatifomo ley yi tlhela yi pfumelela vakomberi ku kuma nkarhi wo tiyisisa tihakelo leti endliweke hi RAF eka vayimeri va vona va nawu.

src: The turnaround strategy has resulted in major improvements in the settlements of claims within 120 days, reduced legal costs by 75 percent and has seen a reduction of medical costs from R.6 billion in the 2019/20 financial year to R.1 billion in the 2023/24 financial year.
tgt: Qhinga ro cinca ri endle leswaku ku va na ku antswisiwa lokukulu eka ku hakeriwa ka swikoxo ku nga si hela masiku ya 120, ku hungutiwa ka tihakelo ta swa nawu hi 75 wa tiphesente naswona ri vonile ku hunguteka ka tihakelo ta vutshunguri kusuka eka R.6 wa tibiliyoni eka lembe ximali ra 2019/20 ku ya eka R.1 wa tibiliyoni eka lembe ximali ra 2023/24.

src: The interventions also led to a cumulative legal costs savings of over R23 billion in the three years of implementing the strategy.
tgt: Ku nghenelela ku tlhele ku yisa eka ku hlayisiwa ka mali leyi hlengeletiweke ya tihakelo ta swa nawu ku tlula R23 wa tibiliyoni eka malembe manharhu ya ku tirhisa maqhinga.

src: Moreover, the strategy interventions resulted in the in the reduction of claims paid to claimants/ short term liability to R.3 billion for the period ending 31 March 2023.
tgt: Ku tlula kwalaho, ku nghenelela ka maqhinga ku endle leswaku ku hungutiwa swikoxo leswi hakeriwaka eka vakomberi/ vutihlamuleri bya nkarhi wo koma ku ya eka R.3 wa tibiliyoni eka nkarhi lowu helaka hi ti31 Nyenyankulu 2023.

src: Cabinet was also updated on legislative amendments to the current RAF Act, which are at an advanced stage.
tgt: Khabinete yi tlhele yi pfuxetiwa hi ku lulamisiwa ka milawu eka Nawu wa sweswi wa RAF, lowu nga eka xiyimo xa le henhla.

src: The RAF Amendment Bill will be considered by the 7th administration of government.
tgt: Ndzulamiso wa Nawumbisi wa RAF wu ta langutiwa hi vufambisi bya vu7 bya mfumo.

src: The bill is aimed at refining the benefits and the payment of certain products in annuities and making it equitable.
tgt: Nawumbisi lowu wu kongomisiwile eka ku antswisa mivuyelo na ku hakeriwa ka swikumiwa swo karhi eka swipfuno swa mali na ku endla leswaku swi ringana.

src: Cabinet decisions White Paper on Citizenship, Immigration and Refugee Protection Cabinet approved the White Paper on Citizenship, Immigration and Refugee Protection for implementation, following a wide consultation process undertaken by the Department of Home Affairs in all nine provinces.
tgt: Khabinete yi pasisile Nawumbisi wa Vuakatiko, Vuhlapfa na Nsirhelelo wa Vahlapfa ku tirhisiwa, endzhaku ka endlelo ro anama ra ku burisana leri endliweke hi Ndzawulo ya Timhaka ta Xikaya eka swifundzankulu hinkwaswo swa kaye.

src: The policy aims to provide a framework to guide citizenship, immigration and refugee protection, considering the country’s national security interests and in compliance with international agreements and protocols on migration that South Africa is party to.
tgt: Pholisi yi kongomisa ku nyika rimba ro letela vuakatiko, vuhlapfa na nsirhelelo wa vahlapfa, ku tekela enhlokweni ku tsakela ka vusirheleri bya rixaka bya tiko na ku landzelerisa mitwanano ya matiko ya misava na tiphrothokholi ta vuhlapfa leti Afrika-Dzonga ri nga xiphemu eka tona.

src: It will also promote South Africa’s economic interests, transformation and job creation efforts.
tgt: Swi ta tlhela swi tlakusa ku tsakela ka ikhonomi ya Afrika-Dzonga, ku cinca na matshalatshala yo tumbuluxa mitirho.

src: Towards a 30-Year Review of South Africa’s Democracy (1994-2024).
tgt: Ku Kongoma eka Nkambisiso wa Malembe ya 30 wa Xidemokirasi xa Afrika-Dzonga (1994-2024).

src: Cabinet approved the publication of the report “Towards a 30-Year Review of South Africa’s Democracy (1994-2024)”.
tgt: Khabinete yi pasisile ku kandziyisiwa ka xiviko lexi nge “Ku Kongoma eka Nkambisiso wa Malembe ya 30 wa Xidemokirasi xa Afrika-Dzonga (1994-2024)”.

src: The review report heralds the story of South Africa’s transition into democracy since the historical elections of 27 April 1994.
tgt: Xiviko xa nkambisiso xi tivisa xitori xa ku cinca ka Afrika-Dzonga eka xidemokirasi ku sukela eka nhlawulo wa matimu wa ti27 Dzivamisoko 1994.

src: South Africa’s story of transition to democracy continues to inspire hope for many people around the world, and the review report highlights important lessons in the evolution of our democracy.
tgt: Xitori xa Afrika-Dzonga xa ku cinca eka xidemokirasi xi ya emahlweni xi hlohlotela ntshembo eka vanhu vo tala emisaveni hinkwayo, naswona xiviko xa nkambisiso xi kombisa tidyondzo ta nkoka eka ku hundzuka ka xidemokirasi xa hina.

src: Over the last 30 years, the country has attained a stable democracy, with strong institutions and a considerable global influence.
tgt: Eka malembe ya 30 lama hundzeke, tiko ri fikelerile xidemokirasi lexi tiyeke, lexi nga na mavandla yo tiya na nkucetelo lowukulu wa misava hinkwayo.

src: The 30-Year Review Report is structured on 13 thematic areas informed by four important references (1) the 1994 Reconstruction and Development Programme and its five objectives (2) the 1996 adoption of the Constitution (3) the 2012 National Development Plan and (4) the Medium-Term Strategic Framework 2019-2024 to reflect seven priorities of the sixth administration.
tgt: Xiviko xa Nkambisiso wa Malembe ya 30 xi hlengeletiwile eka tindhawu ta 13 ta nhlokomhaka leti tivisiweke hi swikombiso swa mune swa nkoka (1) Nongonoko wa ku aka hi Vuntshwa na Nhluvukiso wa 1994 na swikongomelo swa wona swa ntlhanu (2) ku amukeriwa ka Vumbiwa hi 1996 (3) Kungu ra Nhluvukiso wa Rixaka ra 2012 na (4) Rimba ra Maqhinga ra Nkarhi wa le Xikarhi ra 2019-2024 ku kombisa swilo swa nkoka swa nkombo swa vufambisi bya vutsevu.

src: The review report will be published by the Department of Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation and members of society will have an opportunity to engage the report.
tgt: Xiviko xa nkambisiso xi ta kandziyisiwa hi Ndzawulo ya Vupulani, Vulawuri na Nkambisiso naswona swirho swa vaaki swi ta va na nkarhi wo nghenelela eka xiviko.

src: Upcoming Events 6th Commonwealth Red Cross and Red Crescent Conference on International Humanitarian Law South Africa and the International Committee of the Red Cross will co-host the 6th Red Cross and Red Crescent Commonwealth Conference on International Humanitarian Law in South Africa from 15 to 19 April 2024 at the Irene Country Lodge in Pretoria.
tgt: Migingiriko leyi nga ta Landzela Khonferense ya vu6 ya Xihambano xo Tshwuka na N’weti wo Tshwuka ya Nhlangano wa Matiko eka Nawu wa Matiko ya Misava wa Vumunhu.1 Afrika-Dzonga na Komiti ya Matiko ya Misava ya Xihambano xo Tshwuka va ta rhurhela swin’we Khonferense ya vu6 ya Xihambano xo Tshwuka na N’weti wo Tshwuka wa Nhlangano wa Nawu wa Matiko ya Misava eAfrika-Dzonga ku sukela hi ti15 ku fikela hi ti19 Dzivamisoko 2024 eIrene Country Lodge ePitori.

src: The conference will bring together representatives of Commonwealth Member States, members of the Red Cross and Red Crescent movement, and other key stakeholders to deliberate on International Human Law.
tgt: Khonferense yi ta hlanganisa vayimeri va Matiko ya Swirho swa Nhlangano wa Matiko, swirho swa nhlangano wa Xihambano xo Tshwuka na N’weti wo Tshwuka, na vatekaxiave van’wana va nkoka ku burisana hi Nawu wa Vanhu wa Matiko ya Misava.

src: The conference seeks to recalibrate and strengthen existing human rights instruments and deepen our knowledge on the importance of International Human Law in an era of increased armed conflicts as well as climate change, food insecurity and growing displacement.
tgt: Khonferense yi lava ku cinca nakambe ndlela ya maendlelo na ku tiyisisa switirhisiwa swa timfanelo ta ximunhu leswi nga kona na ku dzikisa vutivi bya hina eka nkoka wa Nawu wa Vanhu wa Matiko ya Misava eka nguva ya ku engeteleka ka tinyimpi leti hlomeke xikan’we na ku cinca ka maxelo, ku pfumaleka ka swakudya na ku rhurha loku kulaka.

src: Cabinet extended its congratulations and well-wishes to: Health Minister Dr Joe Phaahla on his appointment to the Global Fund Board effective from 1 May 2024.
tgt: Mahungu Ku hoyozelaKhabinete yi hundzisa mahungu ya yona yo hoyozela ni ku navelela mikateko eka:• Holobye wa Rihanyo Dkd Joe Phaahla eka ku thoriwa ka yena eka Huvo ya Nkwama wa Misava hinkwayo ku sukela hi ti1 Mudyaxihi 2024.

src: Dr Phaahla will serve as a representative of the East and Southern Africa region.
tgt: Dkd Phaahla u ta tirha tanihi muyimeri wa xifundzankulu xa Afrika-Vuxa na Dzonga.• Mamozileme ya MaAfrika-Dzonga xikan’we na lava va nga emisaveni hinkwayo, ngopfungopfu ePalestina, hi xiendlakalo xa Eid al-Fitr.

src: South Africans Muslims as well as those across the globe, especially in Palestine, on the occasion of Eid al-Fitr.
tgt: Ramadan nakambe i nkarhi wa ku anakanyisisa endzeni, ku pfuna na ku tinyiketela ka ximoya loko Mamozileme ya lwela ku kula ka ximoya na ku tikhoma.

src: Ramadan is also a time of inner reflection, charity and spiritual devotion when Muslims strive towards spiritual growth and self-control.
tgt: Nkhuvo wa Eid al-Fitr wu fungha makumu ya n’hweti yo kwetsima ya Ramadan, leyi hi nkarhi wa yona Mamozileme ma titsone swakudya siku na siku, naswona ehansi ka swiyimo swo tika swinene ePalestina.• Khomixini ya Mphikizano ya Afrika-Dzonga hi ku wina masagwadi mambirhi eka Masagwadi ya ku Tsala ya Antitrust ya 2024 leyi khomeriweke eWashington DC na ku xiximiwa eka Vulavisisi bya yona bya Makete bya Tipulatifomo ta Vuhlanganisi bya le ka Inthanete lebyi rhangelaka.

src: The festival of Eid al-Fitr marks the culmination of the holy month of Ramadan, during which Muslims have fasted daily, and under extreme conditions in Palestine.
tgt: Yi hlurile sagwadi eka xiviko xa yona xo hetelela na xiboho kasi sagwadi rin’wana a ri ri ra atikili ya dyondzo eka ku cinca-cinca ka mphikizano eka timakete ta xidijithali ta Afrika-Dzonga eka tendzo na vupfhumba.

src: The first normal Cabinet meeting of the 7th administration took place at the Union Buildings, Pretoria, two days before the country commemorates of the National Women’s Day.
tgt: Nhlengeletano yo sungula ya ntolovelo ya Khabinete ya vulawuri bya vu 7 yi ve kona eUnion Buildings, ePitori, masiku mambirhi loko tiko ri nga se tlangela Siku ra Vavasati ra Rixaka.

src: As we mark the 68th anniversary of the Women’s March and 70 years since the adoption of the Women’s Charter, a declaration of intent by the Federation of South African Women, which clearly defined the rights and privileges for women by women of South Africa.
tgt: Loko hi ri karhi fungha ku tlangela malembe ya 68 ya Machi ya Vavasati na malembe ya 70 ku sukela loko ku amukeriwile Tsalwa ra Vavasati, xitiviso xa xikongomelo hi Nhlangano wa Vavasati va Afrika-Dzonga, lowu hlamuseleke kahle timfanelo na swifundzho eka vavasati hi vavasati va Afrika-Dzonga.

src: This year, we celebrate Women’s Month as we also celebrate the appointment of Justice Mandisa Maya on her trail blazing appointment as South Africa’s first female Chief Justice of the Republic of South Africa.
tgt: Lembe leri hi tlangela N’hweti ya Vavasati, loko hi ri karhi hi tlangela ku thoriwa ka Justice Mandisa Maya eka ku thoriwa ka yena ka mabulandhlela tanihi Muavanyisinkulu wa Afrika-Dzonga wo sungula wa xisati.

src: She also previously served with distinction as the President of the Supreme Court of Appeal since 2017 and was the first woman to hold that position.
tgt: U tirhile eka nkarhi lowu ng hundza hi ndlela yo hlawuleka tanihi Presidente wa Khotonkulu ya Aphili ku sukela hi 2017 naswona a ri wansati wo sungula ku va eka xiyimo xexo.

src: The significance of her appointment can be best understood with this context.
tgt: Noka wa ku thoriwa ka yena wu nga twisisiwa ku antswa eka xiyimo lexi nga laha hansi.

src: According to the International Association of Women Judges: “In 1994, there were approximately 165 judges, 160 of whom were white men, three were black men, and two were white women no black women were judges at that time.
tgt: Ku ya hi Nhlangano wa Matiko ya Misava wa Vaavanyisi va Vavasati: “Hi 1994, a ku ri na vaavanyisi va kwalomu 165, lava 160 wa vona a va ri vavanuna va valungu, vanharhu a va ri vavanuna va vantima, vambirhi a va ri vavasati va valungu a ku ri hava vavasati vavantima lava a ri vaavanyisi hi nkarhi wolowo.

src: As of February 2023, there are 253 judges, comprised of which 113 are women, broken down to 32% black women plus 13% white women making up a total of 45% women representation.
tgt: Ku sukela hi Nyenyanyana 2023, ku na vaavanyisi va 253 wa vaavanyisi lava 113 wa vona ku nga vavasati, va lava aviwaka hi ndlela leyi, 32% wa vavasati va vantima ku katsa na 13% wa vavasati va valungu leswi endlaka ntsengo wa 45% wa vuyimeri bya vavasati.

src: Additionally, the remaining 140 male judges are comprised of 39% black men and 17% white men.”
tgt: Ku engetela kwalaho, vaavanyisi lava nga sala va vavanuna va 140 va vumbiwa hi 39% ta vavanuna va vantima na 17% ta vavanuna va valungu.”Timhaka leti nga eka Mbango Tiolimpiki ta le Parisa ta 2024: Ntlawa wa Afrika-Dzonga.

src: Issues in the environment 2024 Paris Olympics: Team South Africa Cabinet congratulated Team South Africa for proudly representing the country at the Paris Olympics and flying the national flag high with the country in the top 30 nations for total medals received.
tgt: Khabinete yi hoyozerile Ntlawa wa Afrika-Dzonga ku va wu yimele tiko hi ku tinyungubyisa eka Tiolimpiki ta le Paris na ku hahisela mujeko wa rixaka ehenhla laha tiko ri nga eka matiko ya 30 ya le henhla eka nhlayo hinkwayo ya timendlele leti amukeriweke.

src: Cabinet once more congratulates:1.
tgt: Khabinet yi tlhela yi hoyozela:1.

src: Swimming sensation, Tatjana Smith for winning gold in the Women’s 100m Breaststroke and silver in the 200m Breaststroke.
tgt: Muhlamberi wa matimba, Tatjana Smith ku va a winile mendlele ya nsuku eka ku hlambela ko tirhisa Xifuva Ntsena ka Vavasati ka 100m na ya silivhere eka ku hambela ko tirhisa Xifuva Ntsena ka 200m.

src: The Blitzboks for winning bronze in the Men’s Rugby Sevens.
tgt: TiBlitzboks ku va va winile mendlele wa eka Men’s Rugby Sevens.

src: Mountain-biker Alan Hatherly for winning bronze during the Men’s Cross-country Cycling Mountain Bike.
tgt: Mukhandziyi wa xikanyakanya etintshaveni Alan Hatherly ku va a winile mendlele wa bronze hi nkarhi wa Men’s Cross-country Cycling Mountain Bike.

src: Akani Simbine who set a new national record when he secured a 4th place finish in the men’s 100m nail-biting final.
tgt: Akani Simbine loyi a nga seta rhekhodo yintshwa ya rixaka loko a fikelela xiyimo xa vumune eka mphikizano wo hetelela wa 100m wa vavanuna wa lowu a wu tika swinene.

src: South Africa is counted within countries with fastest men.
tgt: Afrika-Dzonga yi hlayiwa exikarhi ka matiko lama nga na vavanuna va rivilo swinene.

src: South Africans are called upon to continue to support Team South Africa which will also be competing in the Paralympic Games that will take place from the 28th August until 8th September 2024.
tgt: Maafrika-Dzonga va komberiwa ku ya emahlweni va seketela Ntlawa wa Afrika-Dzonga lowu nga ta nghenela mphikizano wa Mitlangu ya Tiolimpiki ta Vatsoniwa leyi nga ta va kona ku sukela hi ti 28 ta Mhawuri ku fikela hi ti 8 Ndzati 2024.

src: Economy Rail Infrastructure Cabinet welcomed the introduction of new high-tech trains on the Central Line in the City of Cape Town by the Passenger Rail Agency of South Africa (PRASA), an agency of the Department of Transport (DoT).
tgt: Khabinete yi amukerile ku sunguriwa ka switimela leswintshwa swa thekinoloji ya le henhla eka Central Line eka Doroba ra Kapa hi Ejensi ya Swiporo swa Vakhandziyi ya Afrika-Dzonga (PRASA), leyi nga ejensi ya Ndzawulo ya Vutleketli (DoT).

src: The service has been extended from Nyanga to Mandalay station.
tgt: Vukorhokeri byi ndlandlamuxiwile ku suka eNyanga ku ya exiticini xa Mandalay.

src: The trains utilises modern signaling system from Langa to Mutual Line, to enhance the safety and reliability of the rail service.
tgt: Switimela swi tirhisa sisiteme ya manguva lawa ya swikoweto ku suka eLanga ku ya eka Mutual Line, ku antswisa vuhlayiseki na ku tshembeka ka vukorhokeri bya swiporo.

src: The modern hi-tech features in these trains include automated doors, and CCTVs for each coach are for improved passenger safety.
tgt: Swilo swa manguva lawa swa thekinoloji ya le henhla leswi nga eswitimeleni leswi swi katsa minyangwa ya otomatiki, naswona ti-CCTV ta torokisi rin’wana na rin’wana i ta vuhlayiseki lebyi antswisiweke bya vakhandziyi.

src: Cabinet further commended the recovery of more rail lines part of government’s priority of providing safe, reliable and affordable public transport.
tgt: Khabinete yi tlhele yi ndhundhuzela ku vuyiseriwa ka tindlela totala ta swiporo tanihi xiphemu leswi rhangisiwaka emahlweni swa mfumo swo nyika vutleketli bya mani na mani lebyi hlayisekeke, byo tshembheka byo ka byi nga durhi.

src: UNESCO’s World Heritage Sites Cabinet welcomed the latest addition of the South African human rights and liberation struggle sites in the prestigious list of UNESCO’S World Heritage Sites.
tgt: Tindhawu ta Ndzhaka ya Misava ta UNESCO.1 Khabinete yi amukerile ku engeteleriwa ka sweswinyana ka tindhawu ta timfanelo ta ximunhu na ku lwela ntshuxeko ta Afrika-Dzonga eka nxaxamelo wa ndhuma wa Tindhawu ta Ndzhaka ya Misava ta UNESCO.2 Tindhawu leti vuriwaka timfanelo ta Ximunhu, Ntshunxeko na ku Rivalelana: Tindhawu ta Ndzhaka ya Nelson Mandela, a ti pfuni ku hlayisa ndzhaka ya hina yo hlawuleka ntsena, kambe ti tlakusa tiko ra hina ri tiveka tanihi ndhawu leyi kokaka rinoko ra vaendzi eka Tindhawu ta Ndzhaka ta Misava, hi ndlela yoleyo swi tlakusa vupfhumba na ikhonomi.

src: The sites termed as The Human Rights, Liberation and Reconciliation: Nelson Mandela Legacy Sites, not only help preserve our unique heritage but catapults our country to prominence as a major tourist attraction for World Heritage Sites, thereby boosting tourism and the economy.
tgt: Ti katsa Union Buildings, Constitution Hill, purasi ra Liliesleaf, xitsundzuxo xa Sharpeville, Walter Sisulu Square, 16 Khotavuxika 1976: Switarata swa Orlando West, Univhesiti ya Fort Hare na ZK Mathews House, Mqhekezweni, Waaihoek na Ohlange.4 Komiti ya Ndzhaka ya Misava ya UNESCO yi tsala tindhawu tinharhu ta Middle Stone Age ku lemuka ku hoxa xandla ka nkoka ka Afrika-Dzonga eka ku twisisa laha mahanyelo ya vanhu ya manguva lawa ya sukelaka kona.

src: It includes the Union Buildings, Constitution Hill, Liliesleaf farm, Sharpeville memorial, Walter Sisulu Square, 16 June 1976: The Streets of Orlando West, University of Fort Hare and ZK Mathews House, Mqhekezweni, Waaihoek and Ohlange.
tgt: Tona i Diepkloof Rock Shelter ekusuhi na Elands Bay eKapa-Vupeladyambu, Pinnacle Point Site Complex eMossel Bay na yona yi le Kapa-Vupladyambu na Sibhudu Cave eKwaDukuza, eKwaZulu-Natal.

src: The UNESCO World Heritage Committee further inscribed three Middle Stone Age sites in recognition of South Africa’s significant contribution to the understanding of the origins of modern human behaviour.
tgt: Khabinete yi amukerile Mipimanyeto ya Nhlayo ya Vanhu ya le Xikarhi ka Lembe (MYPE) ya 2024 leyi nga komba leswaku Maafrika-Dzonga va hanya nkarhi wo leha.

src: These are Diepkloof Rock Shelter close to Elands Bay in the Western Cape, Pinnacle Point Site Complex in Mossel Bay also in the Western Cape and Sibhudu Cave in KwaDukuza, KwaZulu-Natal.
tgt: Malembe lama ku languteriwaka ku hanya wona ya tlakukile ku ya eka 66,5 wa malembe ku suka eka 53,6 wa malembe hi 2005 hikwalaho ka mbuyelo wa ku nghenelela ko hlaya ka mfumo loku katsaka ku ndlandlamuxiwa ka ku hangalasiwa ka vutshunguri bya antiretroviral - lebyi nga wun’wana wa minongonoko leyikulu ya vutshunguri bya antiretroviral emisaveni hinkwayo, ku nykiwa ka mitlhavelo na ku hunguteka ka mpimo wa ku fa ka tincece ku suka eka mafu lama ringanyetiwaka ya 57 wa tincece eka 1,000 wa leti nga velekiwa ti ri karhi ti hanya hi 2002 ku ya eka 22,9 eka 1,000 wa leti nga velekiwa ti ri karhi ti hanya hi 2024.

src: Mid-Year Population Estimates Cabinet welcomed the Mid-Year Population Estimates (MYPE) for 2024 which showed that South Africans are living longer.
tgt: Tinhlayo ta vanhu va Afrika-Dzonga sweswi ti hundza 63 wa timiliyoni, ku tlakuka ka 1,33 wa tiphesente kusukela hi Mawuwana 2023 ku fikela hi Mawuwana 2024.

src: Life expectancy has increased to 66,5 years from 53,6 years in 2005 as a result of multiple government interventions that included the expanded rollout of antiretroviral therapy - which is one of the largest antiretroviral therapy programme in the world, the provision of vaccinations and the decrease in the infant mortality rate from an estimated 57 infant deaths per 1,000 live births in 2002 to 22,9 per 1,000 live births in 2024.
tgt: Ku kula nhlayo ya vanhu loku pfuxetiweke ku ta pfuna mfumo eka mapulanelo ya wona na maavelo ya swipfuno loko hi ya emahlweni hi antswisa vutomi bya Maafrika-Dzonga hinkwawo.

src: Safety and Security Fight against Crime Cabinet welcomed the continued successes of law enforcement agencies in the arrest of members of organised crime syndicates and gangs as part of the ongoing fight against crime.
tgt: Khabinete yi amukerile ku humelela loku yaka emahlweni ka tiejensi to hlayisa nawu hi ku khomiwa ka swirho swa mitlawa ya vugevenga lebyi kunguhatiweke hi vukheta na ti genge tanihi xiphemu xa ku lwisana na vugevenga loku yaka emahlweni.

src: Operation Shanela of the South African Police Service has also ensured the arrest of 766 237 suspects for various crimes, and 161 752 of these were suspects wanted for priority crimes, including murder, cash-in-transit heists, armed robberies, rape, car hijacking amongst others.
tgt: Operation Shanela ya Vukorhokeri bya Maphorisa ya Afrika-Dzonga na yona yi tiyisise ku khomiwa ka 766 237 wa vaehleketeleriwa va vugevenga byo hambanahabana, naswona 161 752 wa vona a ku ri vaehleketeleriwa lava a va laveriwa vugevenga lebyi rhangisiwaka emahlweni, ku katsa ku dlaya, ku phangiwa ka mali leyi nga eku fambisiweni, ku phanga va hlomile, ku pfinya, ku tekeriwa mimovha exikarhi ka byin’wana.

src: Cabinet welcomed the shutting down of an illegal military training camp in White River, Mpumalanga following an intelligence-driven multidisciplinary law enforcement operation which has also resulted in the arrest of 95 Libyan nationals.
tgt: Khabinete yi amukerile ku pfariwa ka kampa ya vuleteri bya masocha leyi nga riki enawini eWhite River, eMpumalanga leswi nga landzelaa matirhelo ya swiyenge swo hambanahambana swa vahlayisi va nawu lama veke kona hikwalahoka mitirho ya vunhlorhi leswi nga endla leswaku ku khomiwa 95 wa vaakatiko va Libya.

src: Cabinet has reiterated a call to all South Africans to partner with law enforcement agencies in the fight against crime without resorting to vigilantism.
tgt: Khabinete yi vuyelerile xikombelo eka Maafrika-Dzonga hinkwawo xo tirhisana na tiejensi to hlayisa nawu ku lwisana na vugevenga handle ko veka nawu emavokweni ya vona.

src: Cabinet has taken a dim view of actions by some community leaders that amounted to threatening of learners and teachers at their school.
tgt: Khabinete yi alelana na swendlo swa varhangeri van’wana va miganga leswi fanaka na ku xungeta vadyondzi na vadyondzisi exikolweni xa vona.

src: The Department of Basic Education will continue to work with the SAPS to ensure schools remain safe spaces for learning and teaching.
tgt: Ndzawulo ya Dyondzo ya Masungulo yi ta ya emahlweni yi tirhisana na SAPS ku tiyisisa leswaku swikolo swi tshama swi ri tindhawu leti hlayisekeke to dyondza na ku dyondzisa.

src: Fraud and Corruption Cabinet is pleased with the conviction and sentencing, by the Durban Specialised Commercial Crimes Court, of former officials of the Department of Home Affairs and foreign nationals who were found guilty of committing fraud and corruption against the immigration system.
tgt: Khabinete yi tsakisiwe hi ku voniwa nandzu na ku gweviwa, hi Khoto yo Hlawuleka ya Vugevenga bya Mabindzu ya le Durban, ka khale ka vatirhi va Ndzawulo ya Timhaka ta Xikaya na vaakatiko va matiko mambe lava nga voniwa nandzu wo endla vuxisi na vukungundzwana eka sisiteme ya vuhlapfa.

src: The successful convictions bolster government’s efforts of building an ethical, professional, and capable developmental state.
tgt: Ku voniwa nandzu ku tiyisisa matshalatshala ya mfumo yo aka mfumo wa nhluvukiso lowu nga na matirhelo lamanene, wa xiphurofexinali, no va na vuswikoti.

src: Updates to Cabinet Water Security Cabinet was briefed about the initiatives underway to ensure water security in the country given the increasing demand for water due to population and economic growth, and the fact that 75% of available surface water resources in South Africa have already been captured.
tgt: Khabinete yi tivisiwile hi mayelana na matshalatshala lama nga ku endliweni yo tiyisisa ku va kona ka mati etikweni tanihileswi ku nga na ku tlakuka ka ku laveka ka mati leswi vangiwaka hi ku kula ka rixaka na ikhonomi, na mhaka ya leswaku 75% ta swipfuno swa mati lama kumekaka ehenhla ka misava eAfrika-Dzonga swi tekiwile.

src: Currently, there are 14 major national surface water resources infrastructure projects to the value of more than R100 billion in different stages of development.
tgt: Sweswi, ku na 14 wa tiphurojeke letikulu ta rixaka ta swipfuno swa mati lamakumekaka ehenhla ka misava ta ntsengo wo tlula R100 wa tibiliyoni eka switeji swo hambana swa nhluvukiso.

src: The Department of Water and Sanitation has established a Water Partnerships Office together with SALGA and the DBSA aimed at assisting municipalities to drive initiatives to diversify and develop alternative water resources to ensure water security into the future.
tgt: Ndzawulo ya Mati na Mbhasiso yi simekile Hofisi ya Ntirhisano wa Mati na SALGA na DBSA lowu kongomisiweke eka ku pfuna timasipala ku fambisa matshalatshala yo hambanyisa na ku hluvukisa swipfuno swin’wana swa mati ku tiyisisa ku va kona ka mati eka nkarhi lowu taka.

src: Cabinet was also updated about the progress to ensure water supply to the residents of Givani and Hammanskraal and addressing the sewerage spills in the Emfuleni Municipality.
tgt: Khabinete yi tlhele yi tivisiwa hi mayelana na ku ya emahlweni no tiyisisa mphakelo wa mati eka vaaki va le Giyani na va le Hammanskraal na ku ololoxa ku halaka ka thyaka ra nkululo eka Masipala wa Emfuleni.

src: Cabinet was informed that water has started to flow to nine (9) villages under the Greater Giyani Municipality and a further 15 villages will receive water by end of August 2024.
tgt: Khabinete yi tivisiwa leswaku mati se ma kona eka switandi swa nkaye (9) ehansi ka Masipala wa Greater Giyani na leswaku switandi swo engetela swa 15 swi ta kuma mati hi ku hela ka Mhawuri Masipala wa Xifundza xa Mopani wu kumile nyiko ya mali yo pfuxeta no engetela vuswikoti bya Water Treatment Works.

src: The Mopani District Municipality has received grant funding to refurbish and increase the capacity of the Giyani Water Treatment Works.
tgt: Ndzawulo, hi ku tirhisana na City of Tshwane na Magalies Water yi le ku kunguhateni ka projeke ya Magalies Water ku nyika xihlovo xin’wana xa mati yo tenga eHammanskraal eka City of Tshwane hi October 2024, loko City of Tshwane yi ya emahlweni yi lunghisa na ku pfuxeta Rooiwal Wastewater Treatment Works.

src: The Department in collaboration with the City of Tshwane and Magalies Water are completing a Magalies Water project to provide an alternative source of drinking water to Hammanskraal in the City of Tshwane by October 2024, whilst the City of Tshwane continue to repair and upgrade the Rooiwal Wastewater Treatment Works.
tgt: Hi ku vona mitlhontlho leyi yaka emahlweni ya mphakelo wa mati etikweni, DWS yi ta nyika switiviso mavhiki mambirhi man’wana na man’wana hi ku humelela ko ololoxa ku pfumaleka ka mati na magoza lawa miganga yi faneleke ku ma teka ku tiyisisa ku va kona ka mati etikweni ra hina leri kayivelaka mati.

src: Given the increasing challenges of water supply in the country, the DWS will provide fortnightly briefings on progress with addressing water insecurity and measures the communities must undertake to ensure water security in our water scarce country.
tgt: Gezi.1 Mphakelo wa gezi wa nkarhi hinkwawo sweswi wu le kusuhi swinene hikwalaho ka ku tirhisiwa loku tiyeke ka Pulani ya Matirhelo ya Eneji (EAP) leyi tivisiweke hi Presidente Cyril Ramaphosa hi Mawuwana 2022.

src: Electricity The supply of consistent electricity is now a step closer due to the steadfast implementation of the Energy Action Plan (EAP) announced by President Cyril Ramaphosa in July 2022.
tgt: Ku kongomisa ka nkarhi hinkwawo ka EAP eka nhlayiso lowu kunguhatiweke na ku tirha ku fikelela ku va kona ka eneji hi ku tisa vuswikoti bya vutumbuluxi lebyintshwa swi hoxe xandla swinene eka mphakelo wa gezi wa nkarhi hinkwawo na ku ka ku nga vi na ku timiwa ka gezi hi ku siyerisana ku ringana tin’hweti to hlayanyana.

src: The EAP’s consistent focus on planned maintenance and work to achieve energy security by bringing onboard new generation capacity has contributed greatly to consistent power supply and no load-shedding over several months.
tgt: Leswi i swa nkoka leswi tisaka ku kula ka ikhonomi naswona swi na nkucetelo lowunene eka nkoka wa vutomi leswi pfumelelaka vaaki ku ya emahlweni na migingiriko ya vona ya siku na siku va nga kavanyetiwi hi nchumu.

src: Eskom recorded an Unplanned Capability Loss Factor (UCLF) of 8 321 MW at the end of July 2024, signaling a historic milestone in the improvement of electricity generating at its power stations.
tgt: .2 Eskom yi rhekhodile Swivangelo swa ku Lahlekeriwa lo ku nga Kunguhatiwangiki ka Vuswikoti (UCLF) ka 8 321 MW eku heleni ka Mawuwana 2024, leswi kombisaka xendleko xa matimu eka ku antswisiwa ka vutumbuluxi bya gezi eka switichi swa yona swa gezi.3 Khabinete yi hoyozele Eskom hi leswi yi nga fikelela xendleko lexi xa nkoka na ku hlohlotela Maafrika-Dzonga ku ya emahlweni va tekelela vutomi byo hlayisa eneji ku sirhelela giridi ya hina ya rixaka.

src: By doing so we all play our part in helping to keep the lights on, which is crucial to business, industry and the economy.
tgt: Hi ku endla tano hinkwerhu hi endla xiphemu xa ntirho wa hina wo pfuna ku hlayisa mavoni ya voninga, leswi nga swa nkoka eka mabindzu, indasitiri na ikhonomi.

src: Trade 21st AGOA FORUM Cabinet was appraised of the successful participation of South Africa’s delegation in the 21st Africa Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) Forum in the United States as a positive confirmation of good bilateral relations between our country and the USSouth Africa continues to advance a case for the renewal of the Africa Growth and Opportunity Act, which expires in 14 months, and supports calls by African Trade Ministers for the US government to do away with the annual reviews of AGOSA – EU citrus disputes in the WTO Cabinet was also briefed about a formal dispute the country initiated with the World Trade Organisation against the European Union’s (EU) stringent and unnecessary plant health requirements regarding Citrus Black Spot (CBS) and False Codling Moth (FMC) regulations on the export of South Africa’s citrus products to the EU South Africa is the world’s second largest exporter of citrus and 33% of SA’s citrus exports are destined for the EU market.
tgt: Mabindzu.1 21st Foramu ya AGOA Khabinete yi kamberiwile hi ku nghenelela loku hetisekeke ka vurhumiwa bya Afrika-Dzonga eka Foramu ya Nawu wa ku Kula ka Afrika na Nkateko (AGOA) ya vu 21 eUnited States tanihi ku tiyisisa ka kahle ka vuxaka bya matiko mambirhi exikarhi ka tiko ra hina na USA,2.

src: South Africa’s industry provides direct employment for over 140, 000 people in rural South Africa and thus supporting over million people.
tgt: Afrika-Dzonga ra ha yisa emahlweni mhaka ya ku pfuxetiwa ka Nawu wa ku Kula ka Afrika na Nkateko, lowu nga ta fika emakumu endzhaku ka tinhweti ta 14, naswona ri seketela swikombelo swa Vaholobye va Mabindzu va Afrika eka mfumo wa Amerika ku herisa ku kambisisiwa ka AGOA ka lembe na lembe.

src: The measures imposed by the EU, while not a ban, result in significant costs for the SA citrus industry, which are estimated at R2 billion (US$110 million) per year.
tgt: Mikwetlembetano ya SA – EU ya malamula eka WTKhabinete yi tlhele yi tivisiwa hi nkwetlembetano wa ximfumo lowu tiko ri wu sunguleke na Nhlangano wa Mabindzu ya Misava ehenhla ka swilaveko swo tika leswi nga lavekiki swa rihanyo ra swimilani swa Nhlangano wa Yuropa (EU) hi mayelana na swinawana swa Citrus Black Spot (CBS) na False Codling Moth (FMC) mayelana na ku rhumeriwa ka swikumiwa swa Afrika-Dzonga swa malamula ku ya eka EAfrika-Dzonga i tiko ra vumbirhi hi vukulu leri xaviselaka matiko yale handle malamula naswona 33% ta malamula ya SA lama xaviseriwka matiko ya le handle ya kongomisiwa eka makete wa EIndasitiri ya Afrika-Dzonga yi nyika mitirho yo kongoma eka vanhu vo tlula 140, 000 ematiko-xikaya ya Afrika-Dzonga hi ndlela yoleyo yi seketela vanhu vo tlula wa timiliyoni.

src: The EU has decided to impose the stringent measures against South Africa whilst not requiring the same from countries with similar situations such as Israel.
tgt: Magoza lama vekiweke hi EU, hambi leswi ya nga ri ku yirisiwa, ya endla leswaku ku va na ku durheriwa lokukulu eka indasitiri ya SA ya malamula, leyi ringanyetiwaka eka R2 billion (US$110 million) hi lembe.

src: International Relations Cabinet welcomed the ICJ’s Advisory Opinion on the Legal Consequences arising from the Policies and Practices of Israel in the Occupied Palestinian Territories which unanimously affirmed that Israel’s continued presence in the Occupied Palestinian Territories is unlawful under international law.
tgt: Khabinete yi amukerile Mavonelo ya Vutsundzuxi ya ICJ mayelana na Switandzhaku swa Nawu leswi sukaka eka Tipholisi na Mitolovelo ya Israel eka Tindhawu ta Palestina leti Tekiweke leswi tiyisiseke hi ku pfumelelana leswaku vukona bya Israel lebyi yaka emahlweni eka Tindhawu ta Palestina leti Tekiweke a byi le nawini ehansi ka nawu wa matiko ya misava.

src: The judgement creates an additional legal obligation for all states to end complicity in Israel’s illegal actions and to act to ensure respect for international law.
tgt: Vuavanyisi byi nyika vutihlamuleri byo engetela bya nawu eka matiko hinkwawo ku herisa ku seketela swendlo swa Israel leswi nga riki enawini na ku teka goza ro tiyisisa ku xiximiwa ka nawu wa matiko ya misava.

src: South Africa was amongst 49 UN member states that delivered a statement on the matter to the ICJ in February 2024.
tgt: Afrika-Dzonga a ri ri rin’wana ra matiko ya 49 lama nga swirho swa matiko ya UN lama nga yisa xitatimende hi mayelana na mhaka leyi eka ICJ hi Nyenyenyana 2024.

src: Unrests in Kenya and Nigeria Cabinet raised concerns with the continuing unrests in Kenya and Nigeria and urged all parties to find urgent solutions to the plight of citizens with the high cost of living, which South Africa is not spared from.
tgt: Khabinete yi kombisile ku vilerisiwa hi ku pfumaleka ka ntshamiseko loku yaka emahlweni eKenya na le Nigeria naswona yi khutaze mavandla hinkwawo ku kuma swintshuxo swa xihatla swa xiyimo xo tika xa vaaki xa ku durha ka swilo, lexi Afrika-Dzonga na yona yi hlanganaka na xona.

src: United Kingdom’s General Elections Cabinet once more congratulated Prime Minister Sir Keith Sthrmer of the United Kingdom and the Labour Party in their victory in the recent general elections.
tgt: Khabinete yo hoyozela nakambe Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer wa le United Kingdom na Labour Party eka ku hlula ka vona eka nhlawulo wa mani na mani lowa ha ku vaka kona.

src: South Africa stands ready to work with the government of the United Kingdom to increase to increase trade and partnership.
tgt: Afrika-Dzonga yi tshama yi tilulamiserile ku tirhisana na mfumo wa United Kingdom ku engetela mabindzu na ntirhisano.

src: Government will continue to monitor developments in other countries that are also holding elections this year.
tgt: Mfumo wu ta ya emahlweni wu veka tihlo eka leswi nga ta endlaka eka matiko man’wana lama nga ta va na mihlawulo lembe leri.

src: South Africa’s Candidature to multilateral bodies Cabinet has endorsed the South Africa’s candidature to multilateral bodies: The candidacy of Ms Swazi Bajabulile Tshabalala for the Presidency of the African Development Bank (AfDB) for the term 2025-2030, at the elections taking place in August 2024.
tgt: Vuyimelaulangwa bya Manana Swazi Bajabulile Tshabalala eka Hofisi ya Presdiente wa Bangi ya Nhluvukiso wa Afrika (AfDB) eka theme ya 2025-2023, eka nhlawulo lowu nga ta va kona hi Mhawuri 2024.

src: The candidacy of Ms Yvette van der Merwe for the President of the Organisation of Vine and Wine (OIV) at elections to be held in France in October 2024.
tgt: Vuyimelakulangwa bya Manana Yvette van der Merwe bya Presidente wa Nhlangano wa Mirhi ya Vhinya na Vhinyo (OIV) eka hlhawulo lowu nga ta khomeriwa eFrance hi Nhlangula 2024.

src: South Africa has a bid for re-election to the Human Rights Council for 2026-2028.
tgt: Afrika-Dzonga yi bidela ku hlawuriwa nakambe eka Huvo ya Timfanelo ta Ximunhu ya 2026-20.

src: South Africa seeks the re-election of its candidates, Profssor Frans Jacobus Viljoen to the UN Human Rights Advisory Committee for the period 2025-2027, at elections scheduled for October 2024 in New York, USSouth Africa is also seeking terms on the UN’s Commission on the Status of Women (CSW) in 2025 and the Commission for Social Development in 2025.
tgt: Afrika-Dzonga yi lava ku hlawuriwa nakambe ka vayimelakulangwa va yona, Professor Frans Jacobus Viljoen eka Komiti ya UN yo Tsundzuxa ya Timfanelo ta Ximunhu ya 2025-2027, eka nhlawulo lowu nga khomiwa hi Nhlangula 2024 eNew York, eUSA.. Afrika-Dzonga yi tlhela yi lava titheme eka Khomixini ya UN ya Xiyimo xa Vavasati (CSW) hi 2025 na Khomixini ya Nhluvukiso wa Vanhu hi 2025.

src: Elections for both bodies will take place in April 2025.
tgt: Mihlawulo ya mihlangano leyimbirhi yi ta va kona hi Dzivamusoko Afrika-Dzonga yi ta tlhela yi lava ku hlawuriwa eka Huvo ya Vusirheleri ya UN ka theme ya malembe mambirhi ya 2031-2032, loko ku ta va ku ri nkarhi wa Tikonkulu ra Afrika.

src: South Africa will seek elections to the UN Security Council for a two-year term for the period 2031-2032, when it will be the turn of Southern Africa.
tgt: Afrika-Dzonga yi ta teka xiyimo xa Vupresidente bya G20 kusukela hi ti 1 ta N’wendzamhala 2024 Khabinete yi kumile xitiviso mayelana na ku lulamisela Vupresidente bya Afrika-Dzonga bya G20 na ku rhurhela Nhlengeletano ya G20 hi Komiti ya Vaholobye yi nyikiwile vutihlamuleri byo lulamisela ntirho lowu hi ku yimela mfumo na Maafrika-Dzonga.

src: Preparations for South Africa’s Presidency of the G20 South Africa will take over the Presidency of the G20 from the 1st of December 2024 Cabinet received an update on the preparations for South Africa’s G20 Presidency and the hosting of the G20 Summit in 2025.
tgt: Afrika-Dzonga yi ta ya emahlweni yi tirhisa mikateko leyi ku rhangela na ku rhurhela tifaramu ta matiko ya misava to fana na G20 ku kokela rinoko ra misava hinkwayo eka mitlhontlho ya nhluvukiso leyi afrika yi langutaneke ya yona na matiko lamakulu swinene ya le edzongeni wa Afrika (China, India, Indonesia, Brazil na Pakistan.

src: 1 Women’s Month The country will commemorate the 2024 National Women’s Day on 9 August 2024 at the Dennis Nel Stadium, Poffader in the Northern Cape under the theme: “Celebrating 30 years of democracy towards Women’s Development”.
tgt: Rixaka ra hina ri tsundzuka vavasati vo hundza 20 000 lava nga machela eUnion Buildings hi ti 9 Mhawuri 1956, va alelana na ku hundziseriwa ka Milawu ya Mapasi ek vavasati.

src: This year’s celebration of Women’s Month will take stock of progress made on socio-economic empowerment of women since the advent of democracy and the achievements of the objectives of the Women’s Charter.
tgt: Khabinete yi rhamba vaakatiko ku va xiphemu xa mitirho ya n’hweti leyi nga ta katsa na nkombiso wa mabindzu, mivulavurisano yo nyiketana na ku kombisa mikateko leyi nga kona ka vavasati eka tisekitara to hambanahambana leti nga na nkoka eka ku hunguta ku hamabana ka rimbewu.

src: Our nation pays tribute to the more than 20 000 women who marched to the Union Buildings on 9 August 1956, in protest against the extension of Pass Laws to women.
tgt: 2 Nhlengeletano ya Mani na Mani ya Nhlangano wa Matiko ya Misava wa Vutivi bya Tinyeleti (IAU) ya vu 32 Afrika-Dzonga ri rhurhela nhlengeletano leyikulu ya tinyeleti emisaveni hinkwayo, Nhlengeletano ya Mani na Mani ya Nhlangano wa Tinyeleti wa Matiko ya Misava (IAU), ya vu 32 eKapa,2.2 Nhlengeletano leyi yi yi ta khomiwa mavhiki mambirhi ku sukela hi ti 6 Mhawuri 2024 naswona i ro sungula nhlengeletano ya vanhu va swa tinyeleti va matiko ya misava yi va kona eka tikonkulu ra Afrika.3 Ku vulavurisana loku ku na xiave xa nkoka eku pfuneni ka Afrika-Dzonga ku suka eka ikhonomi leyi simekiweke eka swipfuno ku ya eka ikhonomi leyi simekiweke eka vutivi.

src: Cabinet invites citizens to be part of the events of the month which will also include a trade expo, interactive dialogues and showcase opportunities available for women in diverse sectors that are instrumental in narrowing gender disparities.
tgt: Afrika-Dzonga eka malembe lama nga hundza yi ve na ku nghenelela eka nhluvukiso wa tinyeleti na migingiriko leyi fambelanaka na tinyeleti, yi tivisa tiphurojeke letikulu ta sayense to fana na SKA na MeerKAT

src: 32nd General Assembly of the International Astronomy Union (IAU) South Africa is hosting the world’s largest astronomy meeting, the 32nd General Assembly of the International Astronomy Union (IAU), in Cape Town.
tgt: 3 Vhiki ro Hlayisa Mali ra Afrika-Dzonga.1 Vhiki ro Hlayisa Mali ra Afrika-Dzongara (MSWSA) ri ta sungula hi ti 26 Mhawuri 2024 ku fikela 1 Ndzati 2024 ri katsa minongonoko na magoza yo dyondzisa hi timali lama kongomisiweke eka vaxavi.2 MSWSA i goza ra Komiti ya Dyondzo ya Timali ya Vaxavi ya Rixaka (NCFEC) ro hlohlotela, ku nyika matimba na ku dyondzisa Maafrika-Dzonga na ku hoxa xandla eka vaakatiko lava nga na vutivi bya swa timali.3 Migingiriko ya nkarhi wa pfhumba yi ta katsa miletalavutivi ya mahala, ku andlala, miphikizano na mitlangu no kombiswa ka tiburende, mikombiso na tiwebina.

src: Issues in the environment Building a Safer South Africa Fight Against Crime.
tgt: Xiyimo xa Khabinete eka timhakankulu Ku aka Afrika-Dzonga leri Hlayisekeke.

src: Cabinet welcomed the arrest of a 40-year-old suspect believed to be one of the ringleaders behind a kidnapping-for-ransom syndicate that is targeting businesspeople in South Africa.
tgt: Khabinete yi amukerile ku khomiwa ka muehleketeleriwa wa malembe ya 40 hi vukhale loyi ku tshembiwaka leswaku hi un’wana wa varhangeri endzhaku ka ntlawa wa ku tekela vanhu ku kuma nkutsulo lowu kongomisaka eka van’wamabindzu eAfrika-Dzonga.

src: He is also suspected to be a key figure in the R300 million crystal meth drugs seized recently at the Johannesburg suburbs of Fourways and in Bruma.
tgt: U tlhela a ehleketeleriwa ku va munhu wa nkoka eka swidzidziharisi swa khirayisitali methe swa R300 wa timiliyoni leswi nga khomiwa sweswinyana exifundzheninkulu xa Joni xa Fourways na le Bruma.

src: This arrest underscores government’s commitment to decisively deal with organised crime.
tgt: Ku khomiwa loku ku kandziyisa ku tinyiketela ka mfumo ku tirhana hi xiboho na vugevenga lebyi hlelekeke.

src: Cabinet supports the deployment of multidisciplinary law enforcement teams to deal with the high crime rate situation that is prevailing in the Eastern Cape.
tgt: Khabinete yi seketela ku rhumeriwa ka swipano swo sindzisa nawu swa swiyenge swo hambana ku tirhana na xiyimo xa mpimo wa le henhla wa vugevenga lexi nga kona eKapa-Vuxa.

src: The multidisciplinary teams include anti organised crime, specialised operations and intelligence operatives.
tgt: Swipano swa swiyenge swo hambana swi katsa ku lwisana na vugevenga lebyi hlelekeke, matirhelo yo hlawuleka na vatirhi va vuhlayiseki.

src: Cabinet reiterated to law enforcement that communities cannot be held ransom by criminals.
tgt: Khabinete yi vuyelerile eka vatirhelamfumo va nawu leswaku miganga a yi nge khomiwi hi nkutsulo hi swigevenga.

src: Cabinet also welcomed the arrest of the suspect found in possession of 34 passports by the Border Management Agency’s (BMA) at the Lebombo Port of Entry to Mozambique.
tgt: Khabinete yi tlhele yi amukela ku khomiwa ka muehleketeleriwa loyi a kumiweke a ri na 34 wa mapasi hi Vulawuri bya Vulawuri bya Mindzilakano eRibuweni ro Nghena eLebombo eMozambique.

src: This is part of continued efforts to stem out illegal immigration criminal syndicates that seek to undermine our border controls and immigration laws.
tgt: Leswi i xiphemu xa matshalatshala lama yaka emahlweni yo herisa tisindikheti ta vugevenga bya vuhlampfa lebyi nga riki enawini leti lavaka ku tekela ehansi vulawuri bya hina bya mindzilakano na milawu ya vuhlampfa.

src: Fighting crime remains a shared responsibility between the police, communities and all sectors and the Cabinet continues urged citizens to work with law-enforcement agencies to combat crime in our communities.
tgt: Ku lwisana na vugevenga swi tshama swi ri vutihlamuleri lebyi avelaniwa exikarhi ka maphorisa, miganga na swiyenge hinkwaswo naswona Khabinete yi ya emahlweni yi hlohlotela vaaki ku tirhisana na tiejensi to sindzisa nawu ku lwisana na vugevenga emigangeni ya hina.

src: Fight against gender-based violence and femicide (GBVF)1.
tgt: Ku lwisana na madzolonga lama simekiweke eka rimbewu na ku dlayiwa ka vavasati (GBVF)1.

src: Cabinet calls on the men of our nation to join the initiative by President Cyril Ramaphosa to take a stand against GBVF by signing the virtual pledge at WEBTOKEN By signing the pledge, men commit to be part of the solution by maintaining positive behaviour and attitudes, and to take responsibility for their actions.
tgt: Khabinete yi kombela vavanuna va rixaka ra hina ku joyina kungu ra Phuresidente Cyril Ramaphosa ku teka xiyimo xo lwisana na GBVF hi ku sayina xitshembiso xa xiviri eka WEBTOKEN Hi ku sayina xitshembiso, vavanuna va tinyiketela ku va xiphemu xa ntlhantlho hi ku hlayisa mahanyelo na mavonelo lamanene, na ku teka vutihlamuleri bya swiendlo swa vona.

src: It also commits the men to never raise a hand against a woman, to treat women as equals, respect their rights, and to treat them with dignity.
tgt: Swi tlhela swi tinyiketela vavanuna leswaku va nga tshuki va tlakusa voko eka wansati, ku khoma vavasati tanihi lava ringanaka, ku xixima timfanelo ta vona, na ku va khoma hi xichavo.

src: Managing GBVF as a collective will result in healthier, safer and more peaceful communities in which women and children can thrive.
tgt: Ku lawula GBVF tanihi nhlengeletano swi ta endla leswaku ku va na miganga leyi hanyeke kahle, leyi hlayisekeke na ku rhula leyi vavasati na vana va nga humelelaka eka yona.

src: Furthermore, Cabinet welcomed the opening of the 65th Centre at the Mitchells Plain Hospital in Cape Town earlier this week to support victims of GBVGovernment’s establishment of the Thuthuzela Care Centres across the country is a response to the urgent need for prevention, response and support for victims of violence, especially women and children.
tgt: Ku ya emahlweni, Khabinete yi amukerile ku pfuriwa ka Senthara ya vu 65 eXibedlhele xa Mitchells Plain eKapa ekusunguleni ka vhiki leri ku seketela vahlaseriwa va GBVKu simekiwa ka Mfumo ka Tisenthara ta Nkhathalelo ta Thuthuzela etikweni hinkwaro i nhlamulo eka xilaveko xa xihatla xa nsivelo, ku hlamula na nseketelo eka vahlaseriwa va madzolonga, ngopfungopfu vavasati na vana.

src: Cabinet expressed concern over the alarming statistics of adolescent pregnancies where children as young as 10 years of age are prematurely becoming parents.
tgt: Khabinete yi kombisile ku vilela hi tinhlayo leti chavisaka ta ku tika ka vantshwa laha vana lava nga ehansi ka 10 ra malembe hi vukhale va nga si vaka vatswari.

src: Cabinet urges society and parents to help solve this challenge by reporting anyone who engages in sex with a minor (a child under the age of 16) as it is a criminal offence.
tgt: Khabinete yi hlohlotela vaaki na vatswari ku pfuneta ku tlhantlha ntlhontlho lowu hi ku vika un’wana na un’wana loyi a endlaka timhaka ta masangu na n’wana lontsongo (n’wana loyi a nga ehansi ka malembe ya 16) tanihileswi ku nga nandzu wa vugevenga.

src: If the country does not work together to address this challenge of teenage pregnancies, women and young girls will continue to be trapped in a vicious cycle of poverty, lack of educational and economic prospects.
tgt: Loko tiko ri nga tirhisani ku lulamisa ntlhontlho lowu wa ku tika ka vantshwa, vavasati na vanhwanyana lavatsongo va ta ya emahlweni va pfaleriwa eka xirhendzevutani xo biha xa vusweti, ku pfumaleka ka ntshembo wa dyondzo na ikhonomi.

src: Pre-release calendar for the publication of the quarterly crime statistics Cabinet noted the pre-release calendar for the publication of the quarterly crime statistics for the 2024-25 year.
tgt: Khalendara ya le mahlweni ka ku humesiwa ya ku kandziyisiwa ka tinhlayo ta vugevenga ta kotara.

src: The crime statistics will be released in August and November 2024, and in February and May 2025.
tgt: Khabinete yi xiyile khalendara ya le mahlweni ka ku humesiwa ya ku kandziyisiwa ka tinhlayohlayo ta vugevenga ta kotara ta lembe ximali ra 2024/25.
